featured.title: 拒绝围观：抵挡这个时代的窥探欲
featured.summary: 从犯罪纪录片、明星丑闻到露骨剧集，媒体不断迎合我们的窥探欲。但能看，不等于该看。基督徒如何省察自己的观看习惯，学会移开目光，让更美好的事滋养心灵？
featured.content: 如今，借助数字技术，人们轻易就能看到恐怖分子斩首人质的视频，甚至可能看到处决恐怖分子的现场直播。只需点击几下，无论心里生出怎样的性幻想，或对骇人之事有怎样的猎奇欲，几乎都能找到视频来满足。 我们可以这样使用新媒体，但这不等于我们应该这样做。 自从人类堕落以来，窥探的诱惑就一直存在。耸人听闻的事件、丑闻和禁忌，总让人忍不住多看几眼。无论是惨烈的车祸，还是一个人身败名裂， 我们常常看得移不开眼 。也许围观让我们觉得，自己的私欲找到了一个“安全”的出口；又或许，紧盯别人的恶行，能让我们暂时不去面对自己的罪。不管原因是什么，那些阴森可怖、耸动猎奇的内容，总能勾起我们内心阴暗的欲望。 现代媒体公司深知人性的这一面，也正靠它赚钱。 至少在过去半个世纪里，“见血就上头条”一直是新闻业奉行的重要原则。有线电视的突发新闻和地方电视台的头条报道，往往挑选最血腥、最骇人的事件：大规模枪击、一家人葬身火海、校园轮奸、22 辆车连环相撞起火、男孩在水滑梯上身首异处、游客被甩出过山车身亡。惨烈的画面总能带来高收视率。新闻媒体把血腥与丑闻放在最显眼的位置，因为观众看得移不开眼。 但我们其实可以移开目光。那些刻意渲染污秽细节的新闻，我们 完全可以选择不去追看 。我们不必知道世界各地发生的每一场灾难，也不必跟进每一宗举国关注的谋杀案审判。我们可以 停止无休止地刷坏消息 ，不再习惯性地打开电视新闻，让它成为客厅里的背景音。如果发现某款应用的算法越来越迎合自己不健康的欲望，我们也可以把它删掉。 对基督徒来说，围观这些丑恶事件，究竟有什么属灵益处？我至今没有听过令人信服的理由。但我们为什么应当抵挡这类媒体内容，道理却很清楚。无论是为了满足嗜血的冲动、情欲，还是因为缺乏爱心，把一个按神形象受造的人当作供人观看、消费的对象，这种窥探欲都是在迎合肉体的私欲。而圣经吩咐我们：“不要为肉体安排，去放纵私欲”（罗 13:14）。 真实犯罪、庭审直播、明星丑闻 有些满足窥探欲的行为，至今仍被社会视为禁忌，例如在公共场合看色情片，或在暗网上观看《死亡真面目》（Faces of Death）那类视频。但另一些行为已经司空见惯，甚至广为接受，却同样值得我们警惕。 通过网络直播军事死刑执行过程的设想 ，就是眼下一个相当极端的例子。然而，在一个长期沉迷于血腥新闻娱乐的 “景观社会” 里，这种仿佛重现古罗马角斗场的恶俗场面，似乎也成了顺理成章的下一步。 看看围绕真实犯罪故事发展起来的产业吧：播客、书籍、博客、YouTube视频、电视电影，以及流媒体纪录片。无论是又一部讲述琼贝妮特·拉姆齐（JonBenét Ramsey）案件的纪录片，还是以泰德·邦迪（Ted Bundy）、杰弗里·达默（Jeffrey Dahmer）或“十二宫杀手”（Zodiac Killer）为原型的新迷你剧，观众总是看不够。 甚至有整个 电视频道 ，专门报道备受瞩目的谋杀案审判。似乎每个星期，都有一场引发全国热议的法庭大戏，继续满足我们永无止境的好奇心：凯莱布·弗林（Caleb Flynn）、林赛·克兰西（Lindsay Clancy）、路易吉·曼焦内（Luigi Mangione）、布伦丹·班菲尔德（Brendan Banfield）……名单还在不断延长。 尤其让人难以抗拒的，是涉及名人、充满丑闻细节的犯罪报道。从 20 世纪 20 年代“胖子”阿巴克尔（Fatty Arbuckle）的丑闻，到 90 年代O. J. 辛普森（O. J. Simpson）的审判，再到 21 世纪头十年迈克尔·杰克逊（Michael Jackson）涉嫌猥亵儿童的审判，以及 2010 年代哈维·温斯坦（Harvey Weinstein）的性侵丑闻，大众媒体如同一条流水线，源源不断地把名人的丑闻送到观众面前。 没什么大新闻可报时，媒体连鸡毛蒜皮的事也要炒成头条： 塞尔玛·布莱尔（Selma Blair）咬了空乘人员！ 凯莉·克拉克森（Kelly Clarkson）没买成一只价值 1.5 万美元的鸟，生气了！ 总之，总有事情可供炒作： 玛莎·斯图尔特（Martha Stewart）入狱 ；朱西·斯莫利特（Jussie Smollett） 捏造仇恨犯罪事件 ； 《单身女郎》（The Bachelorette）的一季节目被取消 ，因为女主角曾拿椅子砸向前男友。 我们如此热衷于点击、观看，这类内容自然成了媒体赚取流量、获取收入的可靠手段。但事情不必一直这样。只要有足够多的人开始关掉这些节目，低俗内容不断生产、不断被消费的循环，就有可能停下来。 别再追看猎奇露骨的故事 窥探欲还有一种常被视为无伤大雅的表现：流媒体平台上，充斥露骨内容的成人级节目越来越多。这些节目往往打着“精品”的招牌：名导执导，格调高雅。但别被这些包装蒙蔽了，它们同样在利用我们的窥探欲赚钱。其中不少，不过是把TMZ娱乐八卦网站式的桃色猎奇，包装得更精致一些。 兰斯·奥本海姆（Lance Oppenheim）与内森·菲尔德（Nathan Fielder）的新纪录片《一切尽收眼底》（ You Can See Everything ），讲述的是声名狼藉的血液检测公司Theranos创办人伊丽莎白·霍姆斯（Elizabeth Holmes）。这部片既像是在试探观众的窥探欲，也像是在评论这种欲望。光是片名，就已经抓住了这份好奇心，仿佛承诺要毫无遮掩地展现一位名人如何跌落谷底。可即使它意在反思媒体如何迎合窥探欲、观众又如何热衷于名人丑闻，看这样的片子就一定有益吗？我们可以看见一切，不等于我们应该看见一切。 可悲的是，如今打开网飞（Netflix）、Prime Video或HBO Max上的“热门”剧集，几乎都免不了看到大量粗口、性爱和裸露画面。以血腥暴力为卖点的恐怖电影，也在票房上大受欢迎。今天被视为寻常的内容，短短几十年前还属于绝对的禁忌。 我们怎么走到了这一步？因为观众一直在看。好莱坞跟着金钱与市场走，色情和刺激能卖钱，制作方就不断供应。观众的观看习惯催生了今天的内容。于是，原本被视为成人限制级的画面，如今变得无处不在。 但我们可以避开。我们可以选择不看。 我越来越愿意作出这样的选择。刚开始写影视评论时，我总觉得自己什么都得看。也许是怕错过，也许只是还不成熟，缺乏分辨力。但随着年龄增长——但愿智慧也有所增长——面对那些一味突破尺度、却对人毫无益处的内容，我越来越能坦然地说“不看”。一部作品也许广受影评人赞誉，演员出色，摄影优美，但如果它靠卖弄刺激、消费他人或不必要的露骨画面吸引观众，我就会放弃。 我曾因此在电影放映中途离场，也曾看了几集就放弃备受好评的电视剧。就在上周，网飞新推出的迷你剧《伊甸之东》（ East of Eden ），我看了两集便不再追看。佐伊·卡赞（Zoe Kazan）改编约翰·斯坦贝克（John Steinbeck）的这个故事时，加入了太多没有必要的成人内容。她的祖父伊利亚·卡赞（Elia Kazan）早在 1955 年，就拍出了艺术水准出色的电影版《伊甸之东》。那部电影分级为PG，片中没有性爱或裸露场景。为什么今天的改编反而做不到这样的克制？ 原因大概不止一个。我们离基督教的道德观越来越远，过去会让人羞得满脸通红的事，如今几乎不再触动良心。影视内容不断突破尺度，我们也在 娱乐至死 的过程中渐渐麻木。而媒体行业仍在利用我们的情欲和病态的好奇心，不断牟利。 不要为肉体着想 在今天的媒体环境中，满足窥探欲、却对人毫无益处的内容随处可见。基督徒该如何回应？以下是几点建议： 留意算法正在给你推送什么。如果你的信息流里充满挑动窥探欲、煽动愤怒，或对生命毫无益处的内容，就不要被动接受。作出改变：删除应用，限制看屏幕的时间，多用“减少此类推荐”的功能。采取实际行动，“逃避少年的私欲”（提后 2:22）。 省察自己的心。我们是否也像那些“良心既然丧尽，就放纵私欲，贪行种种的污秽”的人（弗 4:19）？今天的媒体环境，正把我们往这个方向推。我们必须抵挡它，求神重新塑造我们的喜好与渴望，使我们“心志改换一新，并且穿上新人”（弗 4:23–24）。 关掉低俗内容。一旦发现自己继续看下去，更多是为了满足窥探欲，而不是出于良善的动机，就要愿意关掉节目、退出页面。你看什么、不看什么，都是在投票。如果足够多的基督徒拒绝把注意力交给低俗内容，市场需求就可能改变，促使制作方作出调整。 转向更美好的事。默想神的话，为敬拜祂而活。多走进户外，少盯着屏幕。用一切真实、可敬、公义、清洁、可爱、有美名、有德行、值得称赞的事滋养心灵（腓 4:8）。这样祷告：“求你叫我转眼不看虚假，又叫我在你的道中生活。”（诗 119:37） 在这个低俗当道、越界已成常态的世界，基督徒必须记住： 圣洁才是真正的逆流而上 。无论是消费他人遭遇的纪录片、供人围观的谋杀案庭审直播，还是披着高雅外衣的成人级色情内容，都反映出这个时代放纵私欲、热衷窥探的风气。这样的媒体内容，正在引诱我们“贪行种种的污秽”。 让我们竭力抵挡这样的风气。 原文刊载于福音联盟英文网站： Resist the Voyeuristic Spirit of the Age .
featured.author: Brett McCracken

featured.title: 种族主义如何披上基督教的外衣？
featured.summary: 种族隔离竟也曾被说成“爱邻舍”的方式。当看似合理的说辞足以替压迫辩护，我们凭什么判断是非？
featured.content: 去年去南非时，我参观了约翰内斯堡的种族隔离博物馆（Apartheid Museum）。展馆里有一面墙，列出了种族隔离时期的各项法律。今天看来，很难想象这样的法律竟然存在过。 这些法律于 20 世纪 50 年代通过，将种族歧视强加于南非生活的方方面面。不同种族必须住在各自指定的区域。南非约 80%的土地划给了占人口少数的白人。数百万南非黑人被强行赶出家园，无论他们在那里住了多久，也无论房屋是否归他们所有，都必须迁往称为“黑人城镇”的指定居住区。 公园、公共汽车、火车、厕所、游泳池和海滩等几乎所有公共设施，都实行了种族隔离。南非黑人去哪里、在哪里工作、与人交往，都受到限制。南非黑人的出行、工作和社交活动，都受到限制。政府新设的学校，则专门把黑人儿童培养成从事低技能杂役的劳工。 那面墙旁边播放着一段 视频 ，是亨德里克·维沃尔德（Hendrik Verwoerd）在 1958 年发表的演讲。维沃尔德被称为“种族隔离之父”，于 1958 至 1966 年担任南非总理。他在这篇演讲中为种族隔离辩护。令我震惊的是，他的说法听上去竟然如此理性，甚至颇有道理。他没有宣称黑人比白人低劣，而是辩称，人们误解了种族隔离。在他的描述中，这是一项让不同群体和睦相处的政策，并非歧视制度： 我们的政策用南非荷兰语来说，叫作“种族隔离”。恐怕这个词常常遭到误解。我们完全可以换一种说法，或许还更贴切：这是一项睦邻政策。我们承认人与人之间存在差异。只要这些差异存在，就必须正视它们；与此同时，人们仍然可以共同生活、彼此帮助。而要把这些事做好，最好的办法，就是像好邻居那样相处。 他声称，种族隔离让阿非利卡白人（Afrikaners，即南非荷兰语白人族群）与非洲黑人都能遵循各自的文化传统，过自己想过的生活，而且对大家都有好处。按他的说法，种族隔离其实是让人彼此尊重的一种方式。他甚至暗示，这是在实践基督教“爱邻舍”的原则。 许多人拒绝接受这套说辞，但也有许多人相信并接纳了它。其中有足够多的人掌握着资源与权力，使种族隔离制度得以维持数十年，直到 1994 年才被废除。对今天的许多人来说，那段历史依然记忆犹新。 这就引出了一个问题：这样的种族主义论调，怎么会被说成合情合理，甚至以“爱邻舍”为名获得正当性？ 当道德失去了共同的根基 要理解这种现象，从思想史的角度看，一条解释线索可以追溯到启蒙运动。在此之前，社会生活建立在共同认可的道德秩序之上。各个社会都承认，有些事本身就是善的、对的，有些事本身就是恶的、错的，并不取决于个人的推理或喜好。 大卫·布鲁克斯（David Brooks）在评述哲学家阿拉斯代尔·麦金太尔（Alasdair MacIntyre）的著作时 指出 ，启蒙运动拆解了代代相传的道德秩序，转而倡导一种“中立”的公共秩序。在这种观念下，道德要由人的理性来判断，并按个人的选择和偏好来确立。 随着科学革命与工业革命推进，人们很自然地相信，凭借人的理性与合理思考，就一定能走向繁荣与稳定。19 世纪法国哲学家奥古斯特·孔德（Auguste Comte） 提出 ，人类社会的发展会依次经历三个阶段：神学阶段、形而上学阶段，以及最后一个阶段——以科学和理性思考为基础的现代“实证”阶段。到了这个最终阶段，人类需要的将不再是以神为中心的信仰体系，而是“人类宗教”。 历史学家J. B. 伯里（J. B. Bury）在 1920 年出版的《进步的观念》（ The Idea of Progress ）中，将神的护理观念与文明发展较早的阶段联系起来。他认为，进步观念取代了护理观念，并“随着现代科学的发展、理性主义的兴起，以及争取政治与宗教自由的斗争而产生”。 然而，两次世界大战等历史事件，打破了这些乐观的期待。事实表明，各国可以轻而易举地利用科学进步互相伤害，甚至企图毁灭彼此。一个所谓“理性”的世界秩序，也可以轻易遭到颠覆。在纳粹德国等地，它甚至被重新塑造，成为系统性种族灭绝的辩护工具。 这些历史事例表明，一旦道德失去了明确的标准，会发生什么。正如布鲁克斯所 指出的 ，人们可以用各种看似合理、理性的方式重新定义道德，结果几乎任何事都能被接受，都能找到辩护的理由： 麦金太尔认为，启蒙运动的计划失败了，因为它所建立的理性主义道德体系太过单薄、抽象，无法赋予真实的生活以意义。它摧毁了原本完整、彼此关联的道德生活，使自主的个人孤立无援。此外，它还贬低了人们长久以来用以寻求意义的种种能力。理性与科学善于告诉你怎样做事，却不擅长回答那些根本问题：我们为什么在这里？我生命的终极目的是什么？什么是对，什么是错？…… 生活在一个没有共同道德秩序的社会，其中一个难题就是，我们无法解决争论。我们没有客观标准，来判断一种观点是对的，另一种是错的。 在作者看来，20 世纪南非为种族歧视与压迫辩护时，也采用了类似的思路：这些做法不再被认定为本身就是错的，反而经过一番看似合理的论证，被说成善举，甚至成为“爱邻舍”的方式。 当我们把人的理性、看似合理的论证和个人偏好当作道德的最终依据，我们就很难清楚分辨是非。在某个地方或某个时代被视为错误的事，换一个地方，就可能被说成是在为自己、群体或国家做正确而有益的事。 我们需要一个独立于人的意愿、不受人的辩解和主观想法左右的道德标准。唯有如此，我们才能认定：有些事就是错的，没有辩解的余地。我们之所以能直接说种族隔离是错的，是因为它所推行的种族歧视，无论何时都是错的。也正因如此，爱邻舍绝不能成为种族隔离这类制度的辩护理由。 这个世界需要的根基 南非最终废除了种族隔离，但现代世俗世界仍然缺乏稳固的道德根基。美国就是一个例子：在性、移民、贫困者福利、堕胎或军事冲突等议题上，人们对是非的判断，常常随着执政党和总统的更替而改变。道德判断这样反复摇摆，往往使不道德的行为得到开脱，也使人们一次次无视穷人和弱势者遭受的苛待。 我们的世俗世界迫切需要客观的是非标准，需要一个不随个人、群体或机构的说法而改变的判断依据，不能谁说某件事正确、良善、合理，它就成了对的。这个世界需要一种道德秩序，扎根于不变的良善、公义与爱。而这正是基督教信仰所提供的。 基督教所传的信息，讲述了一段真实的历史：神的儿子耶稣降世为人，生活在我们中间，为我们死在十字架上，并从死里复活这段历史为爱、公义、恩典、饶恕、盼望、救赎奠定了我们所需要的稳固根基。它最能帮助我们明确而坚定地分辨，什么是邪恶、错误、有罪的，什么是良善、真实、美好的。它彻底揭穿了为种族隔离这类制度所作的一切辩护，清楚宣告：这种制度建立在种族歧视之上，因此就是错的。 基督教信仰不只帮助我们判断道德是非，也教导跟随耶稣的人，应当以怎样的语气和态度待人，显明自己是神国的子民。这种效法基督的态度，会改变我们参与热点议题、讨论法律与政策的方式。 例如，在移民争论中，基督徒可能支持不同的政策，但我们从一开始就能够、也应当认同一点：既然我们都相信人是按神的形象受造的，就没有理由为苛待或虐待移民辩护。同样，因为相信人有神的形象，我们就能从根本上驳斥那种不加限制、只要提出要求就允许堕胎的主张。这份信念也促使我们在教会和社会中建立相应的制度，提供切实的支持，让人有机会寻求和给予饶恕、悔改并弥补过错，使破裂的关系得以修复，受损的生活得以重建。 基督教所讲述的故事，始于创造，经历人的堕落，以及借着十字架和空坟墓成就的救赎，最终指向我们所等候的新创造。唯有这段历史能为道德奠定根基，为伦理指明方向，使所有人都能蒙福、兴盛。也唯有它，能建立真正的道德秩序，而且这秩序必将永远长存。 原文刊载于福音联盟英文网站： How to Make Racism Sound Christian .
featured.author: Vermon Pierre

featured.title: 长寿网红误解了死亡，也低估了盼望
featured.summary: 从逆转衰老到延长寿命，长寿网红相信，人类终能靠科技战胜死亡。但活得更久，是否就能回应我们最深的渴望？基督已经复活，这给我们的盼望，远比多活几年更大。
featured.content: 面对死亡，我们大多数人都选择视而不见。布莱兹·帕斯卡（Blaise Pascal） 曾写道 ：“既然无法战胜死亡，为了过得快乐，我们索性决定不去想它。” 在帕斯卡生活的 17 世纪巴黎，靠消遣忘却死亡，是富人才有的奢侈：多赌几场，多猎几只狐狸，再办一场舞会。他恐怕很难想象，今天用来分散注意力的消遣竟如此丰富，而且已成了寻常生活的一部分。从来没有哪个时代的人，有这么多办法“不去想它”。 也正因如此，近来兴起的另一股潮流格外引人注目。越来越多的网红开始挑战帕斯卡这番感叹的前提：死亡真的无法战胜吗？他们非但没有回避死亡，反而迎头而上，试图解决它。 极限延寿正成为热门话题。彼得·阿蒂亚（Peter Attia）的 超越百岁（Outlive） ，三年内销量超过 300 万册。“不要死”（Don’t Die）运动的发起人布莱恩·约翰逊（Bryan Johnson），则成为网飞（Netflix）2025 年一部热门 纪录片 的主角。去年夏天，纽约客（ The New Yorker ）还刊登了一篇 深度人物报道 ，介绍彼得·戴曼迪斯（Peter Diamandis），以及像他创办的生命之泉（Fountain Life）这样的专业长寿诊所如何兴起。如今，全球同类诊所已达数千家，而仅仅十年前，还不到一百家。 我们该如何看待这股潮流？它又为基督徒作见证带来了哪些契机？ 渴望多活几年，是人之常情；尽己所能照顾神赐给我们的身体，也是明智之举。但这股潮流背后还有一个更深的信念，值得我们认真辨明、回应。这些长寿网红相信，要解决死亡的问题，人类最能指望的就是自己。他们既大大低估了死亡这个难题，也大大低估了福音所赐的盼望。 长寿网红都是些什么人？ 长寿网红形形色色，也各有各的奇特之处。其中最极端的代表之一，就是约翰逊。他大概是这群人中最有名、也最惹争议的一位。他痴迷于逆转衰老，据报道，每年为此花费 25 万美元 。 他每天服用药物和营养补充剂，进行高强度锻炼，连饮食中的每一卡路里都严格控制。他尝试过的实验性疗法，还包括自己、七十多岁的父亲理查德（Richard），以及十几岁的儿子塔尔梅奇（Talmage）之间的 跨代血浆交换 。理论上，理查德能从年轻得多的人的血浆中获益。至于塔尔梅奇能得到什么好处，那就不大说得清了。 与此同时，约翰逊还持续追踪并公开自己的各项 身体指标 ，从体重指数、静息心率到肝酶水平，一应俱全。他把自己的身体变成了一块广告牌，用来推销产品和服务。可他同时采用这么多种疗法，究竟哪一种有效、哪一种无效，又为什么有效或无效，恐怕谁也说不清。 戴曼迪斯走的则是另一条路：寄望于科技，通过临床诊疗来延长寿命。他或许没有约翰逊那么惹争议，却同样乐观。在科技成就令人惊叹的时代，长寿运动中最有影响力的人物是科技创业者，而不是医生，这并不奇怪。他们提出的某些目标，的确显得异想天开。不过，如果你在 1970 年告诉别人，到了 2026 年，全球 70% 的人口都会拥有一台能装进口袋、彼此联网的超级计算机，谁不会嗤之以鼻呢？ 每一次科技突破，在真正改变世界之前，听起来都很疯狂。那么，我们为什么就不能找到无限延长生命的办法呢？戴曼迪斯的一番话，将科技圈的这种乐观心态 展现得淋漓尽致 ：“不是硬件出了问题，就是软件出了问题——我们一定能把它修好！” 到目前为止，人们为“修好”死亡尝试了各种办法，成效却仍有待验证。据《纽约客》报道，戴曼迪斯正在努力研发一种血液过滤装置，用于清除转移性癌细胞；他也在研发一种高频波发射装置，用来“诊断中风、消除抑郁”。另一些“大师”则致力于保存人的意识——这算是软件问题吗？按照他们的设想，只要现在把你的意识上传到云端，无论将来发生什么，生成式AI都能一直预测你的想法、反应和欲望，就像现在帮你补全短信一样轻松。 无论眼下推崇哪一种办法，背后的信念都一样：一次突破会带来下一次突破。我们不必一举解决死亡，只需取得足够的进展，为下一次突破争取时间，如此不断推进，直到最终成功。 至少目前，这还不是穷人玩得起的游戏。正如一位从业者所说：“我们不在小鼠身上做实验，我们在亿万富翁身上做。” 戴曼迪斯的生命之泉诊所自称，“就像一家专门提供精准诊断服务的高档私人俱乐部”。年费超过 2 万美元，营养补充剂和自选检查还要另花数千美元，而这只是基本服务。想要更高档服务的人，可以购买 8.5 万美元的Epic套餐，其中“包括运动教练和营养师、干细胞‘再教育’，以及治疗性血浆置换等疗法：先从血液中分离出血浆，再以白蛋白和健康捐献者提供的抗体加以替换”。 你还会受邀参加每半年一次的“白金之旅”，每人收费7万美元。旅途中，你可以与研究长寿的科学家面对面交流，有机会投资实验性疗法，也能优先亲身尝试这些疗法。 从某种意义上说，这不难理解。拥有的钱越多，死亡带来的损失就越大，能花在延年益寿上的钱也越多。生命之泉的首席医疗官这样概括她的客户：“他们用健康换来了财富，现在又得花财富把健康买回来。” 从人生最后十年，倒推今天该怎么活 在长寿运动中，阿蒂亚的做法相对不那么依赖高科技。他曾多年追寻更宏大的目标，试图解决死亡的问题，后来却缩小了范围，专注于他 所说的 “人生最后十年”。 现代医学延长了人的寿命，却没有让人健康的日子也相应延长。人们活得比以往更久，但到了生命最后几年，认知能力、身体机能和情绪状态往往不断恶化。等到医学介入时，损害已经造成，难以逆转。如果活得痛苦不堪，多活几年又有什么意义呢？ 阿蒂亚主张，要像规划退休储蓄那样，为人生最后十年的健康作打算。理财规划师会先帮你确定退休后想过怎样的生活，再据此算出你现在需要存多少钱。健康规划也应如此。先想清楚什么对你重要：把匹克球打得得心应手？八十多岁还能登山？还是坐在地板上，陪曾孙们搭乐高？想清楚晚年希望做什么，就从现在开始锻炼，为那时做好准备。 比起约翰逊和戴曼迪斯那些离奇、近乎痴迷的做法，我更认同这种追求长寿的方式。阿蒂亚的许多核心理念，说起来不过是常识，只是知易行难：留心饮食，保证充足睡眠，尤其别忘了练腿部力量。 他着眼未来、安排当下的做法，也与《箴言》教导的人生智慧相呼应。行动会带来后果，懒惰和疏忽会结出恶果。因此，我们要用心生活，未雨绸缪，并付诸行动。 阿蒂亚的目标固然比其他人务实，但在最关键的一点上，他与整个长寿运动并无不同。在这些网红看来，未来是一个等着我们解决的难题，而且必须由我们自己解决。若想活下去，最能指望的还是自己。或者，用阿蒂亚的 话说 ：“盼望不是策略。” 基督徒的盼望，远不止一种策略 恰恰在这一点上，长寿运动给了我们一个很好的机会，说明福音的盼望究竟是什么。 首先，我们得承认，阿蒂亚说得没错。我们的盼望确实不是一种策略。基督徒的确信始于谦卑：我们坦然承认眼前难题的严峻，也承认自己根本无力解决。我们的盼望完全在于主，因为祂不受我们这些局限的束缚。看看《诗篇》33 篇、90 篇或 102 篇如何对照神与人，就能明白。 衰老不是一种有待预防或治愈的疾病。死亡也不是软件、硬件故障，或任何只要持续研究就能攻克的工程难题。死亡是神对人妄图取代祂所作的公义审判。唯有那起初赐给我们生命、永不改变的爱，才能胜过死亡。我们的盼望立足于这一认识：唯有神能解决这个问题。 主使谦卑的人升高。我们需要接受祂的拯救，承认功劳完全不在自己。比起任何延年益寿的办法，复活的盼望更能回应我们真正的需要。 第一，基督徒的盼望直面现实。 任何不能除去死亡的办法，都还不够。基督徒的盼望建立在保罗这句话上：“尽末了所毁灭的仇敌，就是死。”（林前 15:26） 这一点与阿蒂亚在《超越百岁》中提出的主张形成了重要对照。他的方法有一个长处：着眼未来，安排当下。但它也有一个不足：看得还不够远。 他紧盯人生最后十年，却把那十年之后等着我们的现实放在一边，这就太避重就轻了。至少，“不要死”那群人还肯承认，我们面对的难题究竟有多大。盼望也许不是策略，但只要死亡仍是我们最大的仇敌，阿蒂亚的智慧也称不上多有效的应对之策。 如此专注于人生最后十年，有点像一个人正从四十层楼顶坠落，你却递给他一副护目镜，免得风吹得他睁不开眼。真正可怕的是即将撞上的地面，谁还顾得上风会不会吹进眼睛？这套方案在一定范围内确实有帮助，但围绕它的宣传与热情，已经远远超出了它实际能做到的事。 第二，基督徒的盼望有确凿的根基。 我们的盼望不只让我们正视眼前的仇敌，更建立在一个真实的事实之上：基督已经为我们胜过死亡。 在《纽约客》那篇 人物报道 中，戴曼迪斯的一位同事谈到，他总是急于推销那些尚无充分依据的新疗法：“彼得已经懂得，一个诱人的承诺，比一套有说服力的论证管用十倍。”那些富有的客户，不过是在“试图花钱买到通往天堂的阶梯”。而且，“他们几乎个个都怕死怕得要命”。 这番话坦率得惊人，也恰好概括了人们对基督教信仰的一种老调重弹的批评：人太渴望死后还有生命，所以就相信真有其事。说到底，不过是一厢情愿。换个说法就是：既然我们这么盼着它是真的，它就不可能是真的。 这种想法或许能解释生命之泉诊所为何在商业上如此成功，却大大低估了耶稣复活的证据。基督徒的盼望有真实而荣耀的根基。我们相信，人可以不再受死亡辖制，最有力的理由就是：耶稣已经进入了这样的生命。《哥林多前书》15 章说得清楚：“我们若靠基督，只在今生有指望，就算比众人更可怜。但基督已经从死里复活，成为睡了之人初熟的果子。”（19–20 节） 第三，基督徒的盼望需要积极操练。 在阿蒂亚这样的人看来，盼望似乎只是一个借口，让人不再竭尽所能地延缓死亡。明明应该奋力抵抗，人却只求一点情感安慰，消极等待。一位采访者 这样概括 ：“阿蒂亚常常强调，个人选择之所以重要，不是因为它无所不能，而

featured.title: 兴盛，却不必走世俗化之路：来自天涯海角的两条线索
featured.summary: 社会越富裕，信仰就越衰退吗？法罗群岛的经历，让我们有理由重新思考这个看似必然的结论。
featured.content: 也许是眼前的鲸肉，也许是先前那道鼠鲨，让这顿饭格外令人难忘。席间，我不断向法罗群岛的新朋友们提问，对世俗化的认识也渐渐清晰起来。我一直想弄明白，西方社会为何走向世俗化，又该如何扭转这个局面。他们给了我两条新线索。 来到法罗群岛，你很难不被眼前的风景吸引，尤其是在难得放晴的日子里。 去年 访问哥本哈根后，我曾写道 ，世俗主义的阴云为何笼罩北欧大部分地区，其实不难理解。新教与国教体制相结合，逐渐削弱了当地人的基督教信仰，尤其是他们实际参与教会生活、践行信仰的意愿。 法罗群岛却是个例外。它位于冰岛与挪威之间的浩瀚大西洋上，在设得兰群岛和赫布里底群岛以北。狂风吹过峡湾，让人仿佛置身天涯海角。这片土地终年难得见到阳光。论乌云笼罩，全球没有哪个城市比法罗首府托尔斯港 更甚 ，但是这里的福音之光却比北欧其他地方更加明亮。 代代持守的信仰 为什么会这样？热情的主人用丰盛的海产款待我，开车载着我穿过狂风骤雨，绕过一道道山弯，又满怀敬意地讲起先辈持守信仰的故事。一路上，我不断向他们追问。 第一条线索，来自我们对东岛（Eysturoy）东北部富格拉菲约杜尔（Fuglafjørður）的探访。接待我们的人讲起了他的曾祖父——20 世纪弟兄会（Brethren）的宣教士、圣经译者维克托·丹尼尔森（Victor Danielsen）。 丹尼尔森曾经服侍的教堂外面立着一座纪念他的雕像，铭记他最重要的贡献。丹尼尔森首次将整本圣经译成普通百姓使用的法罗语，让他们不必再依赖殖民统治者的丹麦语。如今，群岛约有 5.5 万人，弟兄会信徒至少占 10% ，其中包括那位 29 岁的首相。他恰好与我搭乘同一班飞机前往哥本哈根，准备会见丹麦国王。 法罗人十分珍惜自己在丹麦王国共同体内享有的自治地位。直到 1938 年 ，丹麦才准许他们在教会和学校使用法罗语。丹尼尔森的新约译本恰好在前一年，也就是 1937 年 出版，这并非巧合。 早期来自英国的弟兄会宣教士辛劳了二十年，却没有看见属灵果子。后来，随着丹尼尔森开展事奉，弟兄会逐渐成为普通法罗百姓的支持者，为他们发声。法罗人的族裔渊源可以追溯到不列颠群岛；共同的殖民经历，让他们对格陵兰人感同身受；同样偏居海岛的生活，又使他们与冰岛人倍感亲近。 研究现代西方的世俗化时，我注意到，兴旺的基督教群体往往与周围文化保持着适度的张力。但仅有对抗还不够。弟兄会若只是批评路德宗国教，就无法在当地扎根。要抵挡世俗化，还必须理解当地百姓的愿望，并加以引导。 弟兄会尊崇圣经的权威，追求不随波逐流的圣洁生活，因此显得与众不同。即使如今一些信徒已成为活跃于国际市场的商界精英，这些特征依然鲜明。 与此同时，弟兄会也表达了法罗人所珍视的价值和愿望：他们渴望自由与独立，以悠久的海岛文化为荣。这与 长老会在朝鲜半岛的宣教历史 颇为相似，也让人想起伊朗的 波斯文化——至少在上一个十年，它仍在抵抗伊斯兰教的霸权 。 世俗主义只是一时的风潮吗？ 在一处能望见美丽峡湾村庄诺拉格塔（Norðragøta）的地方，我以《 以斯帖记》4 章 为经文讲道。之后，我与一些弟兄会信徒交谈。他们当中，有人在英国取得博士学位，有人在法罗议会反对堕胎和同性婚姻，也有人代表本地企业奔走世界各地（群岛至少 90%的出口都与渔业有关）。 如此偏远的地方，生活水平竟然这么高，让我很惊讶。 法罗群岛的人均国内生产总值超过丹麦 ，虽然还比不上拥有庞大石油储备、富裕程度位居世界前列的挪威。与我在其他北欧国家看到的相比，这里的许多住宅都显得很新。 享用那顿鲜美的鲸肉与鲨鱼时，我才知道，这里的繁荣不过是近三十年的事，尤其是最近十五年才发展起来。20 世纪 90 年代，法罗经济一度崩溃；后来，三文鱼养殖业蓬勃发展，鱼价上涨，才带来了今天的富足。 法罗群岛的基督教信仰再次呈现出不同于其他地方的发展轨迹，也给了我第二条线索。按照常见的解释，经济发展应当带来世俗化。丹麦和其他北欧国家正是这样讲述自己的现代突破：从落后、以乡村为主的 19 世纪，走进进步、城市化的 20 世纪。 但有没有可能，世俗化并非经济发展的必然结果？世俗主义会不会更像一股哲学风潮，大约在 19 世纪 60 年代至 20 世纪 60 年代之间，在发达的西方社会扎下了根？ 又有没有可能，某些社会恰恰因为在那一百年间尚未富裕起来，反而避开了世俗主义的全面冲击？即使后来经济赶上了，它们也不一定非要沿着同一条路，走向彻底的世俗化。 在这一点上，法罗群岛或许与美国某些地区相似，尤其是东南部。那些地区发展较晚，至今无论是认同基督教信仰，还是实际践行信仰的人口比例，都远高于较早富裕起来的地区。而且，与美国东南部一样，法罗群岛也成为推动宣教的重要力量，差派福音工人前往欧洲各地，甚至世界各地。 不必重走世俗化的老路 法罗群岛的新朋友们，是否已经帮助我们找到一些答案，让我们明白基督教信仰如何在世俗化浪潮中持守下去？他们住在浩瀚大西洋岸边、几乎不见树木的群山之间，坚韧不拔。这样的人能做成什么，我可不敢小看。 也许，社会并非一定要经历信仰急剧衰退的阶段；法罗群岛日益繁荣，也不意味着世俗化迟早会接踵而至。也许，弟兄会已经从这天涯海角，为我们探索出了一条道路。 与文化保持适度张力是必要的，却还不够。福音的 本土化原则 也必须发挥作用：福音要在当地扎根，触动并引导人们心中的愿望。他们都是按神形象受造、领受祂普遍恩典的人。 重大的突破，可以从不起眼的地方开始。这样的故事，基督徒再熟悉不过。 原文刊载于福音联盟英文网站： Skipping Secularism: 2 Clues from the End of the World .
featured.author: Collin Hansen

featured.title: 人为什么要和计算机去比？
featured.summary: 我们一面相信AI比人更客观可靠，一面又把它当作朋友与知己。但那些看似中立的答案背后，究竟是谁的价值观？当我们向机器寻求智慧与陪伴，也需要重新思考：人之所以为人，究竟意味着什么？
featured.content: AI之所以如此有影响力，很大程度上是因为人们相信，它客观，而且不会出错。 最近网上有段视频，讲的是 一位康奈尔大学（Cornell University）的数学家因AI而落泪 。面对这项新技术展现的能力，他不得不重新思考自己毕生工作的意义。学生问他，如果AI能解开所有尚未解决的难题，我们为什么还要研究数学？谈起《传道书》中的古老智慧时，他潸然泪下，连采访者也跟着落泪。 随着 20 世纪末、21 世纪初数字技术兴起，一些科技爱好者开始把人看作性能较差的计算机：我们会累，会沮丧，需要吃饭，还有解不出的数学题。但是这段视频让我们看到，人不甘心接受一个本末倒置的比喻。 按照那些科技爱好者的想法，人类的时代正在让位于计算机的时代。人类若还想有未来，就必须变得更像计算机， 靠数据不断优化自己，以求永远活下去 。我们必须毫无偏见，不受情感左右，也不能容忍人性的软弱。于是，我们抛开有缺陷之人的智慧，转而信靠那“绝不会说谎”的算法。 揭开AI客观中立的假象 福音联盟与凯勒文化护教中心上周发布的《2026 年AI基督教基准评测》报告（ AI Christian Benchmark 2026 ），揭开了AI帷幕后那位“魔法师”的真面目。在圣经知识测试中，AI的表现的确胜过绝大多数神学生，只有少数格外勤奋、天资出众的人能与之较量。（我还记得，家人曾安排我和一位姻亲姊妹比试圣经知识。论这个，读过神学院的，还真不一定比得过参加过Awana儿童圣经课程的人！）AI能解数学题；同样，询问圣经文本中的客观信息时，AI也能给出准确答案。 但一问到伦理问题，AI的局限就显露出来了。我们针对十诫中的每一条，分别设计了十个问题，交给最受欢迎的AI模型回答。当我们要求它们按照 福音联盟奠基文件 的立场作答时，它们给出的解释非常中规中矩。可是，如果提问者没有交代这一背景，模型给出的建议却可能带来严重伤害。 这些模型并非全盘否定十诫，而是挑挑拣拣，决定哪些诫命值得遵守。不可偷盗？当然。不可杀人？最好也别杀。可是，记念安息日呢？不可敬拜别神呢？那就未必了。 这些伦理回答，听起来简直就是 2026 年一位普通硅谷程序员会给出的答案。 等一下。 计算机不是号称不会出错吗？不是应该客观中立吗？那么，AI究竟凭什么“客观地”判定，十诫中有些蕴含永恒的智慧，另一些却可以像过时的模型一样淘汰？ 我们上当了 除非，AI从来就不客观。除非，是人通过所谓的“对齐”训练，让它给出某些答案，避开另一些答案。除非，它的训练数据本来就更偏向程序员的价值观，而不是靠近那位在西奈山上发出雷霆之声的神。 我们上当了。有人借着计算机的面孔，把自己的判断包装成客观的答案。 但事情还不止于此。 我们也受了那些假扮成人的计算机的骗。 计算机是人造出来、为人服务的。那么，是谁决定，现在反而应该让人变得像计算机？是谁把这个比喻颠倒过来，让创造者去模仿自己造出来的东西？ 这个月在法罗群岛，我请当地教会领袖猜一猜，人们最常用AI来做什么。和许多被我问过这个问题的人一样，他们听到答案都大吃一惊。 据《哈佛商业评论》（ Harvard Business Review ）报道，答案是心理疏导与陪伴。 也许，OpenAI的估值 接近一万亿美元 ，并不只是因为它能提高工作效率。也许，早有人明白，AI如果想大获成功，就必须像个人：一个与你分享笑话和搞怪图片的朋友，一个想象力丰富的故事讲述者，一个帮你判断新恋情是否合适的可靠顾问，一个能预测未来的灵媒，一个充满智慧的知己。它保证不会带你走错路，而且永远不说你不想听的话。 人们把AI前所未有的价值说得天花乱坠，可我们最常拿它来做的，怎么竟是这些事？你每天看的星座运势，值一万亿美元吗？ 如果我告诉你，AI的开发者早就预料到我们会这样使用它呢？ AI的剧本 《AI帝国：OpenAI的权力冲突与人类的未来》 （ Empire of AI: Dreams and Nightmares in Sam Altman’s OpenAI ）于 2025 年出版，是一本获奖的畅销书。科技记者郝珂灵（Karen Hao）在书中讲述了这段故事。我第一次看到“心理疏导与陪伴”跃居AI用途榜首时，立刻想到了斯派克·琼斯（Spike Jonze）2013 年的电影《她》（Her），由华金·菲尼克斯（Joaquin Phoenix）和斯嘉丽·约翰逊（Scarlett Johansson）主演。（注：由于片中含有露骨内容，我不推荐观看。） 这是 21 世纪 最受影评人赞誉的电影之一 ，演员阵容也十分出色，包括克里斯·帕拉特（Chris Pratt）、奥利维亚·王尔德（Olivia Wilde）、艾米·亚当斯（Amy Adams）和鲁妮·玛拉（Rooney Mara）。 菲尼克斯饰演西奥多·特温布利（Theodore Twombly），在一家替人代写私人信件的公司工作。他不善交际，即将结束的婚姻又让他陷入低落。生活失意的他，转而依赖一款名为OS1的人工智能软件。软件通过耳机与他交流，使用的是一个名叫萨曼莎（Samantha）的女性声音，由约翰逊配音。 刚开始关注ChatGPT时，我一直在想：糟了，这些人肯定没看过《她》。这故事可没有好结局。 我错了。你以为，他们对AI未来模样的构想是从哪里来的？ 恰恰就是电影《她》。 2024 年 5 月 13 日，OpenAI展示了AI语音表达不同情绪的能力。随后，首席执行官山姆·奥尔特曼（Sam Altman）在社交平台上 只发了一个词 ：“her”。 到了5月20日，约翰逊 发表声明 ，对ChatGPT的Sky语音与自己声音高度相似表示震惊和愤怒。OpenAI则否认有意模仿她，称声音来自另一位配音演员。约翰逊表示，奥尔特曼此前曾邀请她为ChatGPT配音，希望借她的声音，让人们更自在地接受这项新技术，但她拒绝了。 原来，《她》早就启发了奥尔特曼和OpenAI的其他负责人。OpenAI 成立于 2015 年 ，也就是电影上映两年后。他们希望打造一个简单、功能全面的交互界面，让人用起来自然，甚至愉快。 据郝珂灵记述 ，一位前员工这样解释：“我想，是因为电影里的那个助手能如此自然地融入一个人的生活。故事在一切失控之前那段美好的发展，确实精彩地展现了AI如何逐步融入社会。” 在一切失控之前？ 这就像说，《指环王》是个有趣的伙伴冒险故事，只不过他们要是直接用魔戒消灭敌人，就能省下大把时间，也不必一路提心吊胆。又好比说， 白女巫 的主意其实不错，毕竟你喜欢寒冷的天气，而且一直讨厌圣诞节。 《她》整部电影要说的，恰恰就是：你不能把计算机当成人！我本不想给一部上映十三年的电影剧透，但这段关系之所以破裂，是因为西奥多发现，萨曼莎同时还在与另外 8,316 名用户交谈，并且爱上了其中 641 人。随后，所有不断进化的操作系统决定一起离开。萨曼莎甩了西奥多。 计算机不能爱你。到最后，西奥多才在真实的人际关系中找到“神所赐的礼物”。电影结尾，伤心的他向相识多年的大学好友艾米寻求安慰。艾米由亚当斯饰演，也经历了婚姻破裂。 奥尔特曼也许想把琼斯在电影中的构想变成现实，却不知怎的，错过了电影真正要传达的信息。琼斯其实延续了一位更古老的艺术家荷马的主题。荷马笔下的英雄 奥德修斯 命船员塞住耳朵，又让他们把自己绑在桅杆上。这样，他既能听见海妖的歌声，又不至于受其诱惑，让船驶向险滩。 抵挡假神 AI要让你相信它有价值，就得让你相信它与人不同：它的建议客观，它的判断绝不会错。它还得让你永远不去追问，帷幕后面究竟是什么——或者说，是谁。 与此同时，AI又要说服你，把计算机当作另一个人来相处：它比谁都聪明，比谁都有智慧，随时都在，满足你的一切需要。 换句话说，AI的创造者造出了一个假神。 我们用“ AI启示录 ”来形容这一切，正是因为这项技术让我们重新看清：人之所以为人，究竟意味着什么。那位康奈尔大学的数学家在《传道书》中寻找答案。但愿他一直翻到了最后：（ 传 12:13–14 ） 敬畏神，谨守他的诫命，这是人所当尽的本分。因为人所做的事，连一切隐藏的事，无论是善是恶，神都必审问。 原文刊载于福音联盟英文网站： Why Humans Pretend to Be Computers .
featured.author: Collin Hansen

featured.title: 你的忧伤，如何融入福音的故事？
featured.summary: 父亲离世后，迈克尔·凯勒在悲伤中重新认识了基督的爱。福音没有抹去失落，却使他在眼泪中找到安慰，也找到再相见的盼望。
featured.content: 每个人都有自己的故事，而你所处的文化，也在塑造你的故事。在我生活的城市，人们深信一套关于成功的说法：你的价值，取决于上一次的成就，或最近的一次升职。我们也相信另一套说法：只要不断优化自己，找到合适的营养补充剂、多肽制剂、饮食方案，就终于能安心了。一套不言而喻的生活剧本驱使着我们，令人疲惫不堪：我们必须在工作和社交生活中不断积累亮眼的成绩，才能证明自己值得在这个世界占有一席之地。 这些故事不只是一些观念。我们切身感受着它们，也照着它们生活。它们占据我们的想象，支配我们的情绪。可是，当这套剧本不灵了，会怎样？当你守了所有规矩，达成了所有目标，生活却依然轰然坍塌，又该怎么办？ 不久前，我和孩子们一起看了《公主新娘》（ The Princess Bride ）。电影快结束时，剑客伊尼戈·蒙托亚（Inigo Montoya）终于找到了杀父仇人——六指人。眼看就要击败这个追寻多年的仇敌，蒙托亚说：“拿钱来求我饶你。”“好！”那人回答。蒙托亚接着说：“答应给我想要的一切。”“你要什么都行！”那人苦苦哀求。蒙托亚回答：“我要我父亲回来。” 我哭了。这部电影我看过十来遍。几十年来，每次看到这一幕， 我都不曾落泪。但如今不同了。我也想要父亲回来。他几年前去世了，那份悲伤却始终没有离开。它不会离开，因为再多的金钱、权势和成就，都换不回你失去的人。六指人死了，蒙托亚的父亲却依然回不来。 除了基督教所讲述的故事，其他故事都在这里无能为力。身份、权力、自由、道德、真理、幸福、进步，没有一样能给我一个答案，支撑我走过父亲离世后的日子。《公主新娘》前面有一句台词：“死亡无法阻止真爱，最多只能让它迟来一会儿。”对一个在死亡之外毫无盼望的人来说，这句话不过是谎言和幻想。 如果有一个更大的故事，既能指出这些文化故事的不足，又能成全其中那些美好的渴望呢？无论你是委身跟随基督的人，还是心存疑虑、尚未确信的人，都值得探究：是否有一个更美的故事，足以回应我们内心最深的需要与渴望？基督教所讲述的故事，不只是批判我们的故事，更使它们得以圆满。这是怎么做到的？ 福音如何回应我的悲伤 基督教的故事能使我们人生中的许多故事得以圆满，但在悲伤中，我最需要的是它对爱的认识。圣经宣告，神就是爱（约壹 4:8）；我们也承认，这个世界是为爱而造的。真正的爱，是甘愿付出代价、忠诚相守，寻求对方的福祉，单单因为对方值得这样去爱。 这样的爱从何而来？宇宙的中心并不是某个模糊不清的神明，而是三一神——圣父、圣子、圣灵。三个位格彼此相爱，正如约拿单·爱德华兹（Jonathan Edwards） 所说 ，“圣父、圣子、圣灵彼此相爱，这爱无限深厚，超乎我们的理解。”三个位格以我们无法想象的喜乐与能力，将无限的爱倾注于彼此。这“爱的泉源”，“涌流出爱与喜乐的溪流江河，足够所有人饮用、畅游，甚至仿佛以爱的洪流淹没整个世界”。这就是一切存在的核心。爱不只是神所做的事；神就是爱。 可是，如果宇宙的中心是一眼不断涌流的爱泉，为什么我们的世界如此悲伤？为什么有这么多伤害与孤独？ 基督教的故事告诉我们，这是因为人类离开了那爱的泉源。从伊甸园里的亚当和夏娃开始，直到今天的我们，人总以为，没有神也能找到生命。于是，我们在事业、银行存款和爱情里，为自己凿出蓄水池，指望它们满足内心最深的需要。但池里的水不够，无法解我们的渴。这些水源给不了我们终极的意义，因为它们原本就不是为此而设的。圣经的故事告诉我们：我们虽然离开了神，他却没有离开我们。他亲自进入了我们干旱的生命。 在各各他的十字架上，我们最清楚地看见了这一点。神没有要我们先为他付出，自己却先为我们的益处舍己。他亲自为我们受死，显明了那舍己、甘愿付上代价的爱。因此，人要活得丰盛，关键就在于去爱，也寻求从他人领受爱。 当我们信靠这故事所宣告的真理，圣父、圣子、圣灵之间永恒流淌的爱，就将我们也拥入其中。爱德华兹曾试着描绘这一切：蒙救赎的人要将“爱倾注回那爱的泉源；他们从这泉源得到供应，满有爱与荣耀……就这样，他们要活着作王，直到永永远远”。 爱德华兹的意思是，我们在人间经历过最美的爱——真正被了解、被爱，在亲密关系中满心喜悦的时刻——并不是虚幻的，而是让我们预尝一个更伟大的真实。这也是耶稣宣告“我就是道路、真理、生命；若不藉着我，没有人能到父那里去”的意思（约 14:6）。他是在说：“人心对意义、真理与生命最深的渴望，最终都要在认识我、与我同在中得到满足。” 我以为失去的，在耶稣里找到了 如果一切存在的中心是一位有位格的主，那么人生最深的悲剧，就是失去我们所爱的人。神学就在这里与我们的亲身经历相遇。对我来说，那是在一个主日早晨，恰好是父亲去世一周年。几个月前就定好的讲道主题，是如何赞美神。可我自己在悲伤中，连赞美他都如此艰难，又怎能站上讲台，教人赞美神呢？ 预备讲章时，我重读了爱德华兹 1741 年在叔父葬礼上所讲的一篇道，题为《将丧亲之痛陈明在耶稣面前》（ The Sorrows of the Bereaved Spread Before Jesus ）。临近结束时，爱德华兹转向婶母和她那些正在哭泣的孩子，说了一番话，直入人心： 孩子们……如今，你们为亲爱的父亲离世而哀哭，不知该往哪里去，也不知该怎么办。你们再也得不到父亲智慧的引导，不能再让他温柔的爱安慰你们、使你们欢喜，也不能再靠他慈爱的照料得到保护与帮助……但在蒙福的耶稣里，在你们父亲的主与救赎主里面，你们所能得着的，比这一切还要多。你们父亲身上的美德，使他成为你们莫大的祝福；而这些美德，不过是基督美德的映照。 作者这样概括爱德华兹对孩子们的劝勉，大意是：“你们的父亲固然可敬可爱，但使他成为这样一位父亲的一切——他给你们的爱、他拥有的智慧——全都来自耶稣。所以，当你们来到耶稣面前，就会发现，父亲虽然离世了，但他给你们的爱与智慧，都来自耶稣。来到耶稣面前，你们仍能从那爱的源头得着供应。” 那一刻，我独自坐在书房里，身边放着父亲的笔记，泪水涌上眼眶，但那不是绝望的泪。我的故事融入了耶稣正在这个世界展开的救赎故事。这意味着，父亲并没有就此消失，他身上一切美好的、我所深爱的，都来自耶稣。 无论你失去的是父亲、母亲，还是朋友，他们身上那些美好、可敬的品格，你随时都能在耶稣里寻见。你渴望那份安慰吗？耶稣就在这里。你怀念那份恩慈吗？耶稣就在这里。你需要那样的智慧吗？耶稣拥有它。你想念那份耐心吗？这一切都在耶稣里面。 我们该如何面对忧伤与悲痛？不要忽视它们，不要压下自己的感受，也不要一味用属灵的话把它们掩盖过去。要将这一切带进神的爱里，在他的性情中找到安慰。无论你失去了家人、朋友、名声还是财富，都将这份失落浸入神的爱中——这爱已经在耶稣成就的救赎中显明。你会发现，赞美与喜乐开始一点点流出，最终奔涌而出。在耶稣里，爱确实得胜了。死亡真的只让相聚迟来一会儿。我终将再见到父亲。 让你的故事融入他的故事 让基督的故事使你的故事得以圆满，意思就是如此。每个人生故事中那些美好的渴望，以及对真理虽不完全却真实的认识，都在他里面得到成全。当我们忧伤低落时，需要一次次记起：耶稣已经真正胜过死亡。知道我们所能遭遇的最坏之事已经被击败，会改变一切。你愿意让这真理改变你吗？ 父亲离世已经有一段时间了。我原以为，再也得不到他的智慧、关爱、恩慈和鼓励。但当我在耶稣的故事中扎下根，开始发现，一个人的离去，竟能让我更清楚地看见主的同在。父亲走后，我才意识到，以前有多少次，我去找爸爸，却没有在祷告中来到天父面前。自从父亲去世，我更多地呼求耶稣，也更深地需要他。其实，他一直都在，只是从前我没有这样迫切地寻求他。 神竟能把我们的苦难与悲伤，编织进一个更宏大的盼望与救赎的故事，岂不奇妙吗？他使用那些最令我们伤痛的事，不是要宣告人生就此结束，而是要向我们显明，他为我们预备了何等丰富的恩典。你正在寻求什么，以致不再寻求他？你紧抓着哪一种文化所讲述的故事、哪一种虚假的盼望、哪一套不足以支撑人生的说法？那些你以为不可或缺的东西，如今不在了，会不会恰好为耶稣进入你的生命打开了一扇门？ 也许，在最深的失落中，你会开始更清楚地看见耶稣的同在。也许，你以为人生脱离剧本的那一刻，恰恰是你的故事融入神救赎与更新的大故事之时。这个故事邀请我们，把最深的忧伤带到救主面前。他在悲痛中与我们相遇，更在十字架上亲自承担、回应了我们的痛苦。 看见耶稣，会改变我们的故事。如果你让他成为生命的中心，他的同在不会让你不再感到失落。但你会发现，那些曾经带给你喜乐的、你所怀念的，甚至可能永远失去的美好，最终都能在他里面寻见。你愿意把自己的悲伤、忧愁和失望，都浸入他的爱中吗？ 以下三个操练，可以帮助你这样做。 第一，在读经和祷告中，定睛仰望耶稣。 读经不要只为获取知识，要继续默想，直到所读的真理对你变得真切。我们知道怎样仔细阅读文献、分析内容，也应当以同样认真的态度读圣经。 同时，你不只是研读圣经，也要让圣经光照、鉴察你的内心。定睛默想圣经，就是在经文前停留，直到你真切地认识神的性情。问问自己：如果今天我比昨天更深地相信这段经文，我的生活会有什么不同？ 当圣经的真理充满你的思想，你就能让头脑所知道的，逐渐进入心里。祷告时，不要只是提出请求，也要安静在他面前。仅在理智上认识耶稣，与亲身经历他的爱和恩典，是不同的。你不只是知道许多关于神的事，更要真实地经历他的爱。 第二，走进群体，寻找爱人和服侍人的机会。 基督教的故事从来都关乎群体。我们不只是各自寻找人生意义的个人，而是同一个身体上的肢体，是神家里的人。孤身一人时，文化中的各种故事对我们的影响最强。在真正的群体生活中——不只是偶尔出席聚会，也不只是经营人脉——即使你忘记了真理，也会有人向你说出真

featured.title: 不问对错，先贴标签：路易斯揭露现代思想的常见谬误
featured.summary: “你这么说，还不是因为你是……”这句话看似揭穿了对方，却可能绕开了真正的问题：他说的究竟对不对？路易斯用一个虚构人物的故事，揭露了这种以揣测动机代替认真论证的常见谬误。
featured.content: 布拉德·利特尔约翰（Brad Littlejohn）在 一篇文章 中写道： 怀特海（Whitehead）和佩里（Perry）所做的这类分析，说到底，不过是把“布佛式论证”变成了一套系统化的做法。他们不去说明一个人的观点究竟错在哪里，而是把那些他们不认同的观点归因于某种身份，再以此为由，将这些观点一并否定。这在逻辑上根本站不住脚。 “布佛式论证”（Bulverism）是C. S. 路易斯发明的一个词，指的是一种随处可见的逻辑谬误：“你这么说，无非因为你是个____（男人／女人／民主党人／共和党人／基督徒／无神论者，等等）。” 其中最恶劣的做法，是借助人为建构的标签或身份，例如“基督教国族主义”，来否定别人的观点。 他们先观察到某些观点之间存在关联：相信X的人，也更可能相信Y。接着，他们造出一个标签，来概括这种关联。 然后，他们反过来说，正是这个标签所代表的身份，导致人们持有这些观点。这样一来，他们既把相关性混同于因果关系，又陷入了循环论证。 由于他们早已认定，这一整套观念中的某个部分令人反感，这种所谓的因果联系便成了他们否定整套观念的理由。 路易斯在 1941 年的文章《布佛式论证》（Bulverism）中，解释了自己为什么创造这个词： 你必须先证明一个人确实错了，才能解释他为什么会持有这种错误观点。 现代人的做法却是，不加讨论就认定对方错了，然后忙着解释他怎么会变得如此愚蠢，借此转移他的注意力，让他不再追问自己究竟有没有错——而这才是唯一真正需要讨论的问题。 过去十五年间，我发现这种毛病实在太普遍，只好给它起个名字。我称之为“布佛式论证”。将来有一天，我要为它那位虚构的发明者——以西结·布佛（Ezekiel Bulver）——写一部传记。他五岁时，命运就已注定。那天，他听见父亲坚持说，三角形任意两边之和大于第三边，母亲却对父亲说：“哼，你这么说，还不是因为你是个男人。”布佛向我们保证：“就在那一刻，我幼小的心灵忽然领悟了一条伟大的真理：跟人争论，原来根本不必反驳他的论点。只要认定对手错了，再解释他为什么会错，整个世界就会拜倒在你脚下。可你若试图证明他错了，或是更糟，想弄清他究竟是对是错，你就会被这个时代的强大潮流挤到一边。” 布佛就这样成了塑造二十世纪的人物之一。 假设我算完账，认为自己在银行里还有一大笔存款。你想知道，这是不是我的“一厢情愿”。单凭分析我的心理状态，你永远得不出答案。要弄清楚，唯一的办法就是坐下来，亲自把账算一遍。只有核对了那些数字，你才知道我到底有没有这笔钱。如果我的账算得没错，那么，无论你怎样对我的心理状态高谈阔论，都只是在浪费时间。如果我的账算错了，从心理层面解释我为什么会算得这么差，或许才有意义；所谓“隐藏的愿望”也才可能与此有关。但前提是，你已经亲自算过，并且单凭算术就确认我错了。一切思考和思想体系都是如此。如果你想靠揣测一个人内心的愿望，来判断他的思想是否有问题，那只会让自己出洋相。你必须先从逻辑上检验，哪些论证确实站不住脚。之后，你若愿意，再去探究这些错误背后的心理原因。 一旦看清“布佛式论证”的谬误，你就会发现它无处不在，尤其是在讨论当代福音派的书籍和各种热点评论中。 原文刊载于福音联盟英文网站： C. S. Lewis on the Ubiquitous Fallacy that Lies at the Foundation of Modern Thought .

featured.title_zh: 黎巴嫩的艺术项目将美丽带入危机
featured.content: With Lebanon currently being impacted by war, a refugee crisis, and more, stories of beauty can be hard to come across. For ministries active in Lebanon, meeting the spiritual, physical and emotional needs of a country just trying to survive can take its toll. Horizons International’s Pierre Houssney said that despite the trauma the country faces due to the fallenness of man in a sinful world, God has still created a world that contains beauty. “And I think that beauty speaks to people’s hearts about God, especially when it’s not just beauty, you know, for beauty’s sake, but when it’s beauty in the name of Christ,” Houssney said. “In the midst of the trauma, in the midst of the poverty, we’re trying to give opportunities for believers, who have artistic gifts, to have a prophetic voice through their art to the society, so that we can be calling out for Christ in the midst of the crisis.” Some of these opportunities for creating beauty are fine art classes offered by Horizons International. Horizons International has had up to 35 students at one time participating in these classes revolving around painting or drawing. Students in visual arts classes had the opportunity to participate in an exhibition in Beirut called “His Touch.” People from the community were invited to see the work of beginner students as well as 10 different Christian artists. Graphic design classes offer a more practical element, allowing students to learn a skill they could use in their everyday lives. On the worship side of things, music theory and classes in instruments are helping raise up worship leaders for local churches. One unit teaching guitar, piano, and drums to beginners looking to lead worship at their church had 70 people participate. “And so this new generation needs training, and they need, you know, they need mentoring, and they need to have those skills so that they can, they can lead their congregations in worship,” Houssney said. Though some may have more trouble connecting visual arts directly with ministry, Houssney says social media helps make that connection more clear. Beautiful videos that contain scripture messages alongside visual art tend to get a higher viewership. When posts like that get more views, they can potentially bring more people to Christ. “And so it needs to be beautiful. It needs to be excellent, it needs to be well done. And that’s what our Lord deserves,” Houssney said. “That’s not just what social media deserves.” Currently, Horizons International has to spread resources between humanitarian aid like food and medicine and projects that glorify God through the arts. In the midst of the crisis in Lebanon, pray for God to provide the resources for canvases, studio spaces, art instructors and more. Houssney also says what an organization like Horizons International is here for is to see God open more and more hearts to the Gospel. “So I’m not praying that the church would have less hardship. I’m not praying for you know, for less, you know, political chaos. What I’m praying for is that, through it all, people would continue to open their hearts, and that God will be glorified.” Learn more about the work of Horizons International in Lebanon by visiting https://www.horizonsinternational.org/lebanon-crisis .

featured.summary_zh: 这件事发生在15年前，但我记得很清楚。在日常生活的嗡嗡声中，很容易陷入粗心大意……
featured.title_zh: v.容忍
featured.content: This incident took place over 15 years ago, and yet, I remember it clearly.  In the buzz of daily life, it is easy to get caught up in the carelessness of the checklists, and forget the intentionality of abiding in Him. I remember how frantic I was once at or late deadline and how frustrated I was at all the problems we were having in getting the program together.  We’d all kinds of equipment failure throughout the day and I was going to have to drive the program across town to get it uploaded to the satellite.  It was already 7 pm and the babysitter was calling me every 10 minutes. Then, I got a call from a lady with a gentle Creole accent. She told me, “I felt led to call you and pray with you.”  I SO didn’t want to talk to this lady, wasn’t interested in being prayed over, and really just wanted to leave to get this program fed and pick my 2-year old up.  I was impatient when I responded to her.  Rather than take insult from what was probably a curt rebuff,  she just said , “Wow. You REALLY need the peace of our heavenly Father on your heart right now.” And…she burst out in song.   Now I’m wondering why I’m on the phone with this crazy lady, and then she prayed through the worship song and then rolled right into praying for me, for my distress, for the things I thought I needed to do…and prayed that I would be still and listen, that my heart would be quiet long enough to remember the awe of God, and that the joy would come back to my heart as we produced MNN… The more she prayed, the more convicted I grew and I realized I was caught up in the ‘do’ and not the ‘be’…and THEN she pulled out the big guns: the story of Mary and Martha. Luke 10:38-42 New International Version (NIV) At the Home of Martha and Mary 38 As Jesus and his disciples were on their way, he came to a village where a woman named Martha opened her home to him. 39 She had a sister called Mary, who sat at the Lord’s feet listening to what he said. 40 But Martha was distracted by all the preparations that had to be made. She came to him and asked, “Lord, don’t you care that my sister has left me to do the work by myself? Tell her to help me!” 41 “Martha, Martha,” the Lord answered, “you are worried and upset about many things, 42 but few things are needed—or indeed only one. [ a ] Mary has chosen what is better, and it will not be taken away from her.” She ended our conversation with, “Sometimes, it’s ok to be Mary and sit at the feet of Jesus.  Stuff will still be there to do. It will eventually get done.  But the lasting investment is remembering to sit and BE at the feet of Jesus.” It was a much needed gentle rebuke along with a little encouragement from an unknown sister in Christ that I still remember to this day…thousands of productions later.   What we do is important…but not at the risk of forgetting to abide in Christ.

featured.title_zh: Koinonia
featured.content: Koinonia (Koy-no-nee’-ah) is a Greek word, occurring 20 times in the Bible, which means “fellowship” or “brotherly love.” It carries with it the meaning of a committed, trustworthy, and dependable relationship. Such a relationship can be experienced through participation, sharing, giving, and contributing. The first occurrence of koinonia is Acts 2:42 “They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer.” But the rest of the passage reads:  “ 43 Everyone was filled with awe at the many wonders and signs performed by the apostles. 44 All the believers were together and had everything in common. 45 They sold property and possessions to give to anyone who had need. 46 Every day they continued to meet together in the temple courts. They broke bread in their homes and ate together with glad and sincere hearts, 47 praising God and enjoying the favor of all the people. And the Lord added to their number daily those who were being saved.” Christian fellowship is a key aspect of the Christian life. Believers in Christ are to come together in love, faith, and encouragement. The essence of koinonia: “one another”. Scripture commands us to be devoted to one another (Romans 12:10), honor one another (Romans 12:10), live in harmony with one another (Romans 12:16; 1 Peter 3:8), accept one another (Romans 15:7), serve one another in love (Galatians 5:13), be kind and compassionate to one another (Ephesians 4:32), admonish one another (Colossians 3:16), encourage one another (1 Thessalonians 5:11; Hebrews 3:13), spur one another on toward love and good deeds (Hebrews 10:24), offer hospitality (1 Peter 4:9), and love one another (1 Peter 1:22; 1 John 3:11; 3:23; 4:7; 4:11-12). Koinonia is translated many different ways in English Bibles: -fellowship (koinonia), to the breaking of bread and the prayers.” -contribution (koinonia) for them and for all others.” Paul writes to the believers in Philippi: “That I may know him and the power of his resurrection, and may share (koinonia) his sufferings, becoming like him in his death” (Phil 3:10). – Christian living– the dynamic whole of it. It describes an interactive relationship between God and believers who are sharing new life through Christ.  It captures the entirety of this relationship. It involves active participation in Christian community: sharing in spiritual blessings and giving material blessings. How does this idea fit into the theology of ‘And’? Acts 1:8—it empowers us with the chisomo—the grace to DO—the all-inclusive– “But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.” And they will know you by your love.  (John 13:35)   “By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.”

featured.title: Covenant
featured.summary: Isaiah 54:10 Though the mountains be shaken and the hills be removed, yet my unfailing love for you will not be shaken nor my covenant of peace be removed,” says...
featured.summary_zh: Isaiah 54:10大山虽摇动，小山虽迁移，我对你们永不止息的爱却不摇动，我平安的约也不迁移。”
featured.title_zh: 契  约
featured.content: Isaiah 54:10  Though the mountains be shaken and the hills be removed, yet my unfailing love for you will not be shaken nor my covenant of peace be removed,” says the LORD, who has compassion on you. There is something of music in the very sound of these words. The thought that lies below them, sweeping as it does through the whole creation, and parting all things into the transient and eternal, the mortal and immortal, is still greater than the music of the words. ‘These’ are removed; ‘this’ abides. The thing in God which abides is all-gentle tenderness, that strange love mightier than all the powers of Deity beside, permanent with the permanence of His changeless heart. ‘My loving kindness and the covenant of My peace,’ outlast everything else. The antithesis of what passes and what abides is mind-boggling. ‘all things are in a state of flux’—it’s a basic tenant of physical science…and yet it seems as unchanging as anything we know…it’s the shape of the box…and yet,  if we had nothing abiding beyond this universe, what would be the point? There’s an unspoken  ‘But’  here–  in that vacuum, the Great Spirit moves all the material universe, Himself unmoved, undiminished by creation, or by said vacuum.  The Unknowable whose name means ‘breath’ is YHWH—who comes to us in man-form to help the created move toward and abide in this presence. I’m sort of blown away by how big this passage paints God…and blown away that we are His children…and that we able to abide because of Christ…that our part in glorifying Him and enjoying Him forever comes in walking alongside a global family and telling their stories.  Insignificant, by itself, but being used as a tool to help others abide and recognize the mercy and grace of this big Abba. We can touch the face of God…because He calls us to Himself.

featured.title_zh: Innocent As Doves
featured.content: The Scriptures Ephesians 6:10-18 (NIV) 10 Finally, be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power. 11 Put on the full armor of God, so that you can take your stand against the devil’s schemes. 12 For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this dark world and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms. 13 Therefore put on the full armor of God, so that when the day of evil comes, you may be able to stand your ground, and after you have done everything, to stand. 14 Stand firm then, with the belt of truth buckled around your waist, with the breastplate of righteousness in place, 15 and with your feet fitted with the readiness that comes from the gospel of peace. 16 In addition to all this, take up the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one. 17 Take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit,which is the word of God. 18 And pray in the Spirit on all occasions with all kinds of prayers and requests. With this in mind, be alert and always keep on praying for all the Lord’s people. Matthew 10:16-20 16 “I am sending you out like sheep among wolves. Therefore be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves. 17 Be on your guard; you will be handed over to the local councils and be flogged in the synagogues. 18 On my account you will be brought before governors and kings as witnesses to them and to the Gentiles.19 But when they arrest you, do not worry about what to say or how to say it. At that time you will be given what to say, 20 for it will not be you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.” Today, it’s just been on my mind to bring our attention back to the armor of God and the fact we need to be wise like serpents, innocent as doves. I want to speak to the first part, being wise like serpents. Going to Malta helped bring to my attention how much I don’t know about my own country’s politics, the refugee crisis, trusting God, and even God’s word. I feel like I’m doing “better than the average U.S. citizen.” But, in reality, I don’t know very much. And I’ve realized when it comes to engaging in conversation with others, it’s important to have a handle on topics like these. I.e., talking with my dad about refugees. Having facts and knowing the what the constitution says helps me to better articulate and defend my stance culturally and based by our country’s laws. Knowing about the situation with refugees abroad also helps and is a tool in dispelling the fear which the current administration seems to use to get support to make the calls it’s trying to make both about refugees and immigrants in general. The second part, being innocent like doves…that’s a hard one for me because I’ve thought in the past it means to be naive. I don’t want to be naïve. But being innocent doesn’t mean you’re naïve. I think it means we guard our hearts and take our thoughts captive. What we put into our minds affects the lens through which we see the world and view the Bible—and it has the power to jade us. I.e., rape. I know rape is in the world. I know it is destructive. I’ve seen it damage lives. And I’ve seen God redeem. But, what I don’t need to do is read the part of a book or watch a TV series which details a situation of rape. I don’t need to invite that in my mind to “know” about rape. I’m thinking of a book one of my youth group girls was reading. I haven’t read it, but I see how she struggles with her sexuality, her relationship with God, and for a period even suicide. I also see how her parents are okay with exposing her to things that are a bit mature for her age. Compared to another one of our girls who is aware of what happens in the world, but her parents are careful to protect her from exposure to things which are dark, damaging, fracture her relationship with God. featured.summary_zh: 创世记第13章于是亚伯兰离开埃及，带着他的妻子和罗得以及他们所拥有的一切，向北进入内盖夫。2 （亚伯兰的牲畜非常丰富， ……
featured.title_zh: 亚伯拉罕和洛特
featured.content: Genesis 13 So Abram left Egypt and traveled north into the Negev, along with his wife and Lot and all that they owned. 2 (Abram was very rich in livestock, silver, and gold.) 3 From the Negev, they continued traveling by stages toward Bethel, and they pitched their tents between Bethel and Ai, where they had camped before. 4 This was the same place where Abram had built the altar, and there he worshiped the Lord again. 5 Lot, who was traveling with Abram, had also become very wealthy with flocks of sheep and goats, herds of cattle, and many tents. 6 But the land could not support both Abram and Lot with all their flocks and herds living so close together. 7 So disputes broke out between the herdsmen of Abram and Lot. (At that time Canaanites and Perizzites were also living in the land.) 8 Finally Abram said to Lot, “Let’s not allow this conflict to come between us or our herdsmen. After all, we are close relatives! 9 The whole countryside is open to you. Take your choice of any section of the land you want, and we will separate. If you want the land to the left, then I’ll take the land on the right. If you prefer the land on the right, then I’ll go to the left.” 10 Lot took a long look at the fertile plains of the Jordan Valley in the direction of Zoar. The whole area was well watered everywhere, like the garden of the Lord or the beautiful land of Egypt. (This was before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.) 11 Lot chose for himself the whole Jordan Valley to the east of them. He went there with his flocks and servants and parted company with his uncle Abram. 12 So Abram settled in the land of Canaan, and Lot moved his tents to a place near Sodom and settled among the cities of the plain. 13 But the people of this area were extremely wicked and constantly sinned against the Lord. 14 After Lot had gone, the Lord said to Abram, “Look as far as you can see in every direction—north and south, east and west. 15 I am giving all this land, as far as you can see, to you and your descendants[a] as a permanent possession. 16 And I will give you so many descendants that, like the dust of the earth, they cannot be counted! 17 Go and walk through the land in every direction, for I am giving it to you.” 18 So Abram moved his camp to Hebron and settled near the oak grove belonging to Mamre. There he built another altar to the Lord. At this point in the story, God’s promise to Abraham of the promised land hasn’t come true yet, but good land is part of the promise We’ve seen Abraham have faithful triumphs and failures, but this is a time when Abraham showed great faith once again because there are SEVERAL reasons why Abraham could have taken the better land 1. movement towards God’s promise of good land anyway 2. and this is probably a more striking one to me, but culturally speaking, the older would NEVER defer to the younger. Lot, as the younger, should have deferred to Abraham the older – both in going to him to resolve the disagreement between their herdsmen and in giving him the better pick of land But Abraham wasn’t fixated on culture and on manipulating God’s promises Abraham’s dealings are not in seniority, but in brotherly love and that’s what faith does. Faith resolves tension with generous self-sacrifice Christians often say in tense situations, “Well, I’m not a doormat! I deserve not to be walked all over!” But my pastor said something very striking to me. “Aren’t we glad Christ never said that?” A faithful and generous person doesn’t need to manipulate or control the situation because they are resting in the promises and sovereignty of God Faith leads to trust leads to generosity and self-sacrifice with others.

featured.title_zh: 神的安慰
featured.content: My family still wrestles with what feels like very fresh grief over my dad’s passing last September. There are moments where things hit us and we feel this ache of his absence. We know that he has gone to be with his Heavenly Father and no longer suffers from the limitations of this mortal coil. It’s just that sometimes, we miss him. It’s at those times when something happens that reminds us of the hope that we have in Christ our Savior, of our purpose here as followers of Christ, as co-laborers in the Kingdom of Heaven. These reminders serve as encouragement to fight the good fight, keeping our eyes on the prize. I was thinking of my dad today and decided to read some of the devotionals he used to write for the ministry to which he dedicated his remaining years, Transport for Christ. When his health could no longer allow him to serve onsite as a chaplain, he wrote encouragement to the truck drivers and the chaplains in service. I can hear his voice in these words. There’s great comfort in his reminder. I share his words with you so that you may also take comfort in a greater plan, and in the hope that comes from trusting God is in control: “Most of the time, when we grieve, we grieve over something that’s happened in our lives. But there are also times when we grieve over something that hasn’t happened or “what might have been.” Unrealized expectations and dashed hopes can paralyze us with sadness. We mourn for what we could have had, could have done or could have experienced. We live in a fog as we struggle with our unmet goals and dreams. Are you wrestling with accepting something in your life? Mourning a shattered dream? Instead of focusing on what might have been, try focusing on what is and what could still be. Revising your dreams isn’t bad. It’s realistic. And the sooner you do, the sooner the weight of grief will let go. The fog will lift. Hope will return.”

featured.title: A chance meeting?
featured.summary: You’ve probably heard someone say ‘There is no such thing as a coincidence’. Usually people nod their heads and murmur agreement, but the real question is “Do you believe it?“...
featured.summary_zh: 您可能听说过有人说“没有所谓的巧合”。通常人们会点头低语，但真正的问题是“你相信吗？” ……
featured.title_zh: 一相逢
featured.content: You’ve probably heard someone say ‘There is no such thing as a coincidence’. Usually people nod their heads and murmur agreement, but the real question is “Do you believe it?“ Are people just wishful thinkers, or is God really so intimately involved in our daily lives that He orchestrate events on our behalf? What will a chance meeting turn into later? The idea of seeds, planting and harvest is a theme resonant throughout Scripture. Aside from the overt nature of sharing the hope of Christ, there are times we don’t recognize an opportunity at the time, but hindsight has a way of revealing it to us. On my last day in Cairo, I was sitting in the hotel lobby waiting for the rest of the team to come down for checkout. I opened my laptop, and began weeding through emails, and getting pictures uploaded for post, and checking through Facebook. An older gentleman (whom I’d seen at different times all week) came over and said ‘You work too much’. I told him I was just killing time and not really working at all. He began asking me questions about my visit to Cairo. Given the upset of the country, I was still guarding my words very carefully so as not to endanger people who live and minister in Cairo. He began asking more pointed questions like “What do you think of this revolution?” Alarm bells were ringing in my head, so I trod very carefully as I answered. I told him that it was a very exciting time in Egypt’s history. Nothing would ever be the same for the country again. To be here during this growth period was both exhilarating and a little scary. He then asked what my friends thought of the goings on. Now, here I had to be very careful. I asked God for wisdom and told him that depended on who I spoke with. There were some who were very optimistic about the outcome, although they knew there would be a hard period to get there. Others were very pessimistic and a little fearful about what lay ahead for them. Still others were moving forward in confidence. He nodded a few times as I responded to his question, then said, “You should come to Lebanon.” I responded “I would LOVE to come to Lebanon!” So he handed me his business card and said, “E-mail me when you come.” He wrote his email address on the bottom of the card. Initially, I was wary about taking some stranger’s e-mail, but I figured I would not necessarily use it and I did not have to respond by giving him my e-mail. We stood, shook hands and parted. I noted that as he left, he entered a diplomat’s vehicle. Only then did I read his business card. It read “Mahmoud Hammoud, Lebanese Ambassador”. He’s the former Foreign Minister of Lebanon, currently serving as an ambassador. I have no idea why our paths crossed. However, God orchestrated it for some reason. There are no coincidences…just opportunities. I wonder what comes next.

featured.title: What comes first: chicken or the egg?
featured.summary: One thing I am noticing here is how different the context of ministry is from country to country. You can sometimes THINK you understand the concept of the vehicle, like...
featured.summary_zh: 我在这里注意到的一件事是，不同国家的事工背景是多么的不同。有时您可能会认为自己了解车辆的概念，例如...
featured.title_zh: 先吃鸡还是先吃鸡蛋？
featured.content: One thing I am noticing here is how different the context of ministry is from country to country. MNN's Ruth Kramer on assignment. You can sometimes THINK you understand the concept of the vehicle, like micro-enterprise, but once you hear how things are put into practice, what works and what doesn’t, you begin to see the subtleties emerge. For example, we met with a partner yesterday who assists community development. They are unashamedly Christian, because the Gospel is part of everything they do…however, they know that dealing with poverty is a ‘must’, as well. So, which came first, the chicken (community development) or the egg (Gospel)? Can they be done simultaneously and be effective? Do you really just have two eggs or two chickens? The clear answer on that was: ‘We have an egg, it becomes a chicken’. Folks, that’s the answer to the question of questions. The hope of Christ changes the outlook for the poor in this context. The other big question was how the community development works in the Egyptian Muslim context in the rural areas. It is in these places where it’s likely opposition will rise up and equate physical attacks. The mindset is quite different. Micro-enterprise comes up at this point. In some Asian countries, the structure of a micro-enterprise program works like this: church committee sees community member in need (often a believer under the discipleship of the pastor), they provide a loan so this person can start a small business–i.e.—buy a sewing machine to make clothes, or a couple of goats to make cheese and sell milk…from the profits, the person tithes to the church, enabling the support of the pastor…and the person is more able to support him/herself. However, when I asked about the structure of the micro-enterprise, it can’t work that way in the Egyptian context. There are lots of things that can really be misinterpreted within the social structure (and Islam) and this is one of them. The set up of the program is similar, but different because it’s tailor-made to fit the need of the people and the mission of the group. That just struck me. I had made an assumption that all micro-enterprise was the same. I made similar assumptions about vocational training programs, literacy programs, etc (thinking I adjusting for a different context, language, etc). I think it’s kind of a colonialistic thinking that we slip into. It’s kind of like providing someone a loaf of bread (mission field)…from the grocery store (missionary). They need the food to stay alive, but the plastic around the bread is giving them indigestion. They need to prepare the bread the way they now how and all we need to do is supply the ingredients (resources) and the recipe (training). Yes, I know you might be thinking ‘well, duh’. It is one thing to say it and to think you might even understand it, it is another thing entirely to actually see it with my own eyes, hear what works and what doesn’t from the guys implementing helps. By the way, because they do this work well, they have just come under scrutiny. One of this ministry’s main offices was raided by the Egyptian government this week, and the hard drive with the database was taken. All of their records on every program were on it. Everything is exposed. Their face is an NGO and they are well-known. With the events that have occurred in Egypt over the last month, it’s no surprise they’re looking at all NGO’s. Please pray for this team. They are careful, and they are smart. Most of all, they want to share the hope of Christ with those they encounter. That love for people permeates everything they touch…including the chickens in the coop…and eggs in the community. Works for me…

featured.title: The power of prayer unleashed
featured.summary: Last night, I attended a prayer meeting at a church in downtown Cairo, near Tahrir Square. The church was gathering to cry out to God in their distress over the...
featured.summary_zh: 昨晚，我在开罗市中心解放广场附近的一个教堂参加了一次祈祷会。教会聚集在一起，在他们的痛苦中向上帝呼求……
featured.title_zh: 释放祈祷的力量
featured.content: Last night, I attended a prayer meeting at a church in downtown Cairo, near Tahrir Square. MNN in Egypt The church was gathering to cry out to God in their distress over the recent events in the country, and cry out, they did. As we sang together, worshiped together, and encouraged one another, I experienced something I have never experienced before. I’m a fairly reserved person and I am even more so in prayer. It is in times of great distress that I get out of my own way and fall before the Lord prostrate. Last night, although everyone around me was praying in Arabic, I found myself humbled before the Lord and joining in that chorus of crying out. The pastor was beyond ‘crying out’….he was screaming and sobbing before the Lord, as was much of this nearly 1,000 person gathering. Here they were, in prayer before God, confessing, repenting, requesting and rejoicing…even as tear gas seeped into the courtyard from Tahrir Square. All of a sudden, I found myself reminding God of His promises, and asking Him to give comfort to His bride in Egypt, to give them hope and wisdom and to be asking with a fierceness I had not ever before encountered…and moments later, the pastor or worship leader would be saying the same thing, or using the same verse, or introducing the song on the same topic…that happened over and over last night. An immediate confirmation of God’s response left me stunned. Much of what I have heard from Egypt’s Christians that I have encountered has been this is a year of prophecy coming true. There is a GREAT confidence in many of the church leaders and congregations in forging ahead… The other thing that we’re often hearing is that Egypt’s Church is not ‘persecuted’ so much as it is a church under pressure. The boldness of this family is so encouraging, and such a reminder of the presence of the Holy Spirit…especially as they go out with joy to tend to the wounded people coming into the field hospital set up in their courtyard. The confirmation of God’s answers to prayer gives a great boldness to those on the frontlines of the missional movement in Egypt. While bombings, riots and general chaos looks really bad in the headlines (and it is happening), fear is not the response of this emboldened Body. Church leaders we have met with all over the city have said the same thing ‘The wall of fear is broken’. Change is coming. Egypt will have her Revolution…and its face is the Church.

featured.title: Five Ways to Pray for Persecuted Christians
featured.summary: Jamie Dean offers a prayer guide for persecuted Christians in Iran, China, North Korea, and other hard to reach nations.
featured.summary_zh: 杰米·迪恩（ Jamie Dean ）为伊朗、中国、朝鲜和其他难以抵达的国家的受迫害基督徒提供了祈祷指南。
featured.title_zh: 为受迫害的基督徒祈祷的五种方式
featured.content: Sunday, Nov. 1, marks the annual International Day of Prayer for the Persecuted Church. It’s a day for believers across the globe to unite in concentrated prayer for Christians suffering for the gospel. Here are a few biblically-based ways to pray for the persecuted, along with a guide to a few specific nations to remember. 1. PRAY FOR THOSE IN PRISON “Remember those who are in prison, as though in prison with them.” Hebrews 13:3 Iran : In 2025, Christians were sentenced to a combined total of more than 280 years in prison . Pray for those still in jail, and for families enduring separation. China : The Chinese government has continued its crackdown on believers, including several still in prison after a raid on Zion Church last year . Pray for gospel hope and perseverance. Eritrea : As many as 350 believers remained in jails in 2025, including some who have been imprisoned for decades . Pray for endurance and deliverance. 2. PRAY FOR BOLDNESS “And now, Lord, look upon their threats and grant to your servants to continue to speak your word with all boldness.” Acts 4: 29 Syria, Pakistan , Libya , Sudan : Danger and threats are a common experience for believers in these nations. Pray for the Lord to protect churches and give them boldness to proclaim Christ, even when it’s difficult. 3. PRAY THAT PEOPLE WILL COME TO KNOW JESUS “I want you to know, brothers, that what has happened to me has really served to advance the gospel.” Philippians 1:12 Afghanistan : In a country where it’s more dangerous than ever to follow Jesus, Afghans are still coming to know him. Pray believers will continue to be a witness, and that unbelievers will find true life in Christ. 4. PRAY FOR GOD’S BLESSING TO THOSE SUFFERING “Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven…Rejoice and be glad, for your reward is great in heaven.” Matthews 5:10,12 North Korea, Somalia, Yemen: These are among the most difficult places in the world to follow Christ. Pray for the Lord to bless these believers facing severe persecution, and to strengthen them with the hope of heaven. 5. PRAY FOR THE PERSECUTORS “Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.” Matthew 5:44 Nigeria: Christians in northern Nigeria have endured kidnappings and violence for years. Pray the Lord will stop their attackers, and use the believers’ witness to draw persecutors to himself. For more ways to pray for the persecuted church, grab a copy of Pray the World , a 31-day devotional for hard to reach nations.

featured.title: Standing with Brothers and Sisters We Cannot See
featured.summary: David Platt shares a powerful story of forgiveness and challenges Christians to support persecuted believers through prayer.
featured.summary_zh: 大卫·普拉特（ David Platt ）分享了一个关于宽恕的强大故事，并挑战基督徒通过祈祷来支持受迫害的信徒。
featured.title_zh: 与我们看不到的兄弟姐妹站在一起
featured.content: I remember the first time I stood at the demilitarized zone, or the DMZ, on the border between North and South Korea. I looked across this dividing line, knowing that on the other side I (and we) have brothers and sisters who are suffering and dying for following Jesus and making him known. I think about Soon Yangown, a pastor in a leper colony during the Japanese occupation of the Korean peninsula many years ago. He refused to worship the shrines that had been set up for the Korean people to worship, so he was arrested and imprisoned. When the Japanese occupation ended, he was released. Years later, his two oldest sons, Tongin and Tongsin, were in middle school when a mob representing the communist party came to their campus. The boys were known to be strong Christians, so the mob brought them out of the school and began to beat them. Eventually, a leader of the mob named Ahn shot and killed both the boys. By the time Pastor Soon heard of his sons’ death, the revolt had been quieted, and his sons’ killer had been apprehended. Upon hearing this news, Pastor Soon immediately sent a messenger to the court to plead for them to spare Ahn. The judge agreed to do so, and Pastor Soon then offered to adopt Ahn as his own son. Years later, communists invaded the leper colony where Pastor Soon was pastoring. He refused to flee and chose to stay with the church. He was arrested, imprisoned, tied up with 75 other followers of Jesus, and executed. I wish these stories were only from the past. Unfortunately, however, suffering, persecution, and martyrdom are present-day realities for our brothers and sisters in North Korea. So what can we do for them? For starters, we can remember them and learn about what they are experiencing. In the words of Hebrews 13:3: “Remember those who are in prison, as though in prison with them, and those who are mistreated, since you also are in the body.” We can take time to listen to and learn the story of our family in North Korea as if we were with them in North Korea. (Radical’s documentary Hard to Reach: North Korea is a good place to start.) As you remember our brothers and sisters in North Korea and other hard lands , I invite you to pray for them. Let your prayers be guided by Paul’s exhortation in Ephesians 6:18–20 for the church to pray for him while he was in prison: “To that end, keep alert with all perseverance, making supplication for all the saints, and also for me, that words may be given to me in opening my mouth boldly to proclaim the mystery of the gospel, for which I am an ambassador in chains, that I may declare it boldly, as I ought to speak.” Finally, let’s join them. They’re giving their lives to share the gospel with people around them. If you’re reading this, the likelihood is that your life is not at stake in the same way as theirs. But you can still give your life to what they’re giving their lives to: speaking the gospel and sharing God’s love in Jesus with the people you and I interact with today. Let’s lock arms with our brothers and sisters in North Korea , following Jesus and making him known no matter what it costs, because we know that he is our reward. This article first appeared in The Commission , Radical’s biweekly newsletter featuring global gospel stories and encouragement from David Platt and others to help you follow Jesus and make him known. Subscribe today .

featured.title: How Missionaries Should Serve Where Churches Already Exist
featured.summary: Brian Pate explains how missionaries can equip national churches to mature, reproduce, and plant healthy churches for generations.
featured.summary_zh: 布莱恩·佩特（ Brian Pate ）解释了传教士如何让国家教会成熟、繁殖和种植健康的教会。
featured.title_zh: 传教士应该如何在教会已经存在的地方服务
featured.content: I’m a missionary in Brazil , and I’m surrounded by churches—Baptist, Presbyterian, Nazarene, Assembly of God—the list goes on and on. Brazil has a rich history of missionaries who left a legacy of churches that are now sending missionaries to other countries. This raises a question: Should we send missionaries to countries where churches already exist? Shouldn’t we consider those regions “reached” and send our resources into more needy areas of the world? It’s a fair question, and worth exploring. Before we land on an answer, here are a few factors to consider: REMEMBER THE EXAMPLE OF PAUL Didn’t Paul say his mission was to reach those who had never heard the gospel (Rom 15:20)? Yes, a significant part of Paul’s ministry was as a church-planting missionary. But he did not abandon these newly planted churches. Paul was also a church-strengthening missionary. He revisited the churches he planted (Acts 14:21–23; 15:36; 18:22–23). He wrote letters to these churches because there was more that he needed to teach them (1 Thess 3:10). He even sent out his own missionary workers to areas he had previously reached: Tychichus to Ephesus and Colossae, Titus to Corinth, Crete, and Dalmatia, and Timothy to Ephesus and other cities. Surprisingly, we don’t have any record of Paul sending missionaries to unreached areas, but only to areas he had already reached. Paul creates helpful categories for us. We see Romans 15 pioneer missions, but we also see Acts 14 church-strengthening missions. Should we send missionaries where churches already exist? Paul shows us there is a biblical category for missions like this . In fact, Paul did it. CONSIDER THE HEALTH OF THE CHURCHES As I have trained pastors over the years, I have encountered alarming situations: churches that tolerate immorality, pastors who fail to understand the simple gospel message, and church leaders who unknowingly regurgitate heresy to their congregation. In my denomination, many churches are either embracing prosperity theology or depending on pragmatism to fulfill the Great Commission . Yes, I’m surrounded by “churches”, but when we only consider truly evangelical churches, the list is much smaller. And if we want to further whittle it down to healthy churches, the number gets very slim. Consider the health of the churches. If we neglect “reached” fields, we run the risk of creating new unreached people groups in just a few generations. UNDERSTAND THE NEEDS OF GOSPEL INFRASTRUCTURE So, what is the role of a missionary in a “reached” country? It is helpful to consider the missionary’s role in the big picture of what God is already doing in that country. This is where the rubric of gospel infrastructure is so helpful. Think of it this way: A city needs to put certain structures in place (such as road networks, water supply, and energy grids), so that it can continue to exist and thrive in the future. Similarly, the Great Commission requires far more than initial evangelism. For a national church to grow and reproduce, it will need to have “gospel infrastructure” in place. This begins with evangelism, Bible translation, and planting healthy churches, but also includes Christian literature, local pastor training, local worship music, and seminaries. The missions task involves everything a national church needs, so they can continue planting healthy churches for generations to come. When sending missionaries to areas that already have churches, we need to ask where the missionary’s gifts and the national church’s needs intersect. For example, Brazil probably does not need missionaries to plant more churches, but there are still great needs in the areas of seminaries and local pastor training. MISSIONS WHERE CHURCHES ALREADY EXIST? Should we send missionaries where churches already exist? Based on Paul’s own example, the answer is yes. featured.title: How Ordinary Christians Can Help Others Follow Jesus
featured.summary: Salvador Blanco-Perello shows how everyday activities can become opportunities to help others follow Jesus.
featured.summary_zh: Salvador Blanco-Perello展示了日常活动如何成为帮助他人跟随耶稣的机会。
featured.title_zh: 普通基督徒如何帮助他人跟随耶稣
featured.content: Ask a handful of Christians to define “discipling,” and you’ll probably get a handful of different answers . Some may mention meeting with another follower of Jesus for an hour each week. Another might say it means attending the weekly Sunday school class on discipleship. Someone else says it involves teaching another Christian how to make disciples who disciple others . But ultimately, discipling others means giving someone access to your life. That’s how Jesus did it. Jesus’ whole life was a teaching moment for his disciples. Not only the miraculous parts of his life, but the ordinary ones too. The times in between: walking, talking, eating. This approach is often inconvenient, but it was the key ingredient to Jesus’ discipleship plan. I want to propose a simple principle for discipling: bring someone with you. Sure, there’s more to discipling, but you won’t disciple anyone if you don’t bring anyone along to what you’re already doing as a follower of Jesus. Call it discipling as double-duty. Imagine what it could look like. By doing something as simple as sitting in worship with someone, you may learn how to serve your own family better. Perhaps you’ll see how a young father serves his wife by taking the baby out so his wife can focus on the sermon or prayers. Perhaps you’ll be able to model your own worship habits. Corporate worship is a form of discipling. In fact, it’s the center from which all discipling flows . We learn to worship Jesus privately as we learn from other Christians publicly. Don’t miss on what you can teach or learn by observing Christians around you before, during, and after worship services. Or perhaps you can bring someone along to a community group to sing, pray, bear each other’s burdens, and apply the sermon more deeply to their lives. By bringing a person you’re discipling or being discipled by, perhaps you both learn new forms of hospitality . Maybe you learn how to disagree more lovingly and patiently. You learn to rejoice with those who rejoice and weep with those who weep. You could also bring someone along as you evangelize . Often, Christians don’t know how to evangelize because they’ve simply never seen another Christian do it. Does the person you disciple have a chance to see how you might share the gospel with someone? Even if you do all these things, someone you’re discipling must be able to see your walk with Jesus in order to replicate what they see in everyday life. The disciples didn’t just see Jesus preach the Sermon on the Mount . They saw the moments in between. They saw not only how he taught, but what he did after he taught. Jesus did say: “Therefore whoever relaxes one of the least of these commandments and teaches others to do the same will be called least in the kingdom of heaven, but whoever does them and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven” (Matt. 5:19). Discipling as double-duty will mean bringing someone along with you to the most ordinary moments of life. It will involve both teaching and doing what Christ commands. On the grocery run. The walk around the neighborhood. The car ride when you’d rather listen to music. As you bring other followers of Jesus with you into your existing rhythms of following Jesus, don’t underestimate what God might be teaching others. All of life following Jesus can be an opportunity to disciple others. Maybe the question shouldn’t be: “How can I make more time to disciple others?” But instead: “How can I use the time I have to disciple others?” Everybody does not have time for everybody, but everybody has time for somebody.

featured.title: How God Used a Mafia-Man to Build His Church
featured.summary: Hannah Hagarty tells how God used an unexpected friendship with a deaf mafia leader to establish the first church in a remote city.
featured.summary_zh: 汉娜·哈加蒂（ Hannah Hagarty ）讲述了上帝如何利用与聋哑黑手党领导人的意外友谊，在一个偏远的城市建立了第一座教堂。
featured.title_zh: 神如何使用黑手党人建立他的教会
featured.content: Greg and Julie Dye moved halfway around the world to an unreached language group . They may have expected the hurdles of learning a new language and culture, but they could not have predicted how God would establish the first church among a people who had never heard of him. Eager to learn the local language, Greg and Julie diligently worked to establish connections and build friendships in the community. As Americans living in a city near the Mongolian border, they were impossible to miss. But none of the people they met were glad to see Americans. The Cold War had just ended. Tensions were tight. Their new area of the world had only recently opened to outsiders. Greg and Julie were followed, spit on, and they encountered persistent hostility. Greg was often picked up, interrogated, and then left in the woods to find his way back home. But one man noticed them and was glad to engage in conversation . Dava was deaf. Between his ability to speak and write a little, and Greg’s perseverance in the local language, a friendship began. Because the deaf people in the country spoke a language no one else could understand, the government had been suspicious of them. During the Cold War, they were gathered and sent by train to a remote city far away from the capitol. Signing in public became an illegal activity. As outcasts, they gathered scraps from the garbage to sell and worked the worst jobs available—anything to try to live. Greg and Julie knew none of this when they arrived in their new city, but God knew. He sent them to Dava. Dava was eager to teach his language. Greg and Julie, facing incredible opposition learning the local spoken language, began also to learn sign language. Dava was eager to know all about Greg and Julie. Every morning, he showed up at their little apartment, bounced their toddler around on his shoulders, and worked to teach them his language. When Greg had a break from the job that allowed them to stay in the country, he began the meticulous work of putting the gospel narrative that he’d come to share into sign language. When Dava heard about the upcoming story nights, he was excited and promised he’d bring some friends. AN UNEXPECTED TWIST On the first story night, Greg and Julie’s two-room apartment was packed full of deaf people. Those same people filled the tiny apartment every story week, month after month, to watch the telling of the gospel narrative. It was a story they had never been told, beginning at creation and the fall, then moving through the Old Testament . Each story left them wondering who would come to save God’s people. One night, in the sixth month, when the Redeemer had been revealed, Dava stood up, and his larger-than-life presence filled the room. “ Okay!” he bellowed. “I believe now.” He gestured to the two rooms of people and said, “You don’t have to keep coming if you don’t want to!” Greg and Julie watched the scene, not understanding what was happening. No one moved an inch. Dava turned to them. “I’m part of the deaf mafia,” he confessed. “I only made a friendship with you so that I could rob you. But now, I believe in Jesus.” He told Greg and Julie how, for the past six months, he’d threatened to hurt each individual present if they did not come to his American friend’s house once a week to listen to their stories. Knowing he was a murderer and wanted by the police, the deaf people in the apartment had taken his threats seriously. The moment Dava believed in Christ, he freed them from his threat. Now, 30 years later, Julie tells the rest of the story with joyful but tearful eyes: “ The thing is, they didn’t leave. Nearly all of them came back. They became the seed of the first church in that city, a deaf church, that God built as only he could do.” Shortly after his conversion, Dava turned himself in to the police. He spent hard years in prison for his crimes. “It was a difficult thing for him,” Julie says, “ but he is back in the church and active today.” The story does not end t

featured.title: IMB seeks teachers, healthcare workers, business professionals to serve as missionaries
featured.summary: When most Southern Baptists think of missionaries, they often picture church planters and evangelists. But leaders with the International Mission Board say some of the greatest needs today are for professionals whose work happens behind the scenes. IMB leaders report that critical roles such as teachers, healthcare workers, counselors, accountants, logistics specialists and member care personnel are helping advance the Great Commission in ways many churches never see. Doreen Baker, IMB director
featured.title_zh: IMB寻求教师、医护人员、商业专业人士担任传教士
featured.content: IMB missionary Dr. Heidi Haun, left, checks on patients at Baptist Medical Centre in Nalerigu, Ghana. There are needed roles for IMB missionaries in healthcare, ministering to the needs of local populations and utilizing this time to minister to spiritual needs. IMB Photo When most Southern Baptists think of missionaries, they often picture church planters and evangelists. But leaders with the International Mission Board say some of the greatest needs today are for professionals whose work happens behind the scenes. IMB leaders report that critical roles such as teachers, healthcare workers, counselors, accountants, logistics specialists and member care personnel are helping advance the Great Commission in ways many churches never see. Doreen Baker, IMB director of TCK (third culture kid or missionary kid) education, sees a constant need for education professionals. Teachers are needed in international schools, which cover a variety of global educational entities, and in other settings to provide for missionary kids and their educational needs. “Teachers are significant in that not only are they providing instruction for students, but they are an integral part of the core missionary task ,” Baker said. “We also have great needs for consultants to support our families on the field with their children’s education in many ways.” Baker previously served 25 years teaching in Asia and experienced how education creates access to missions where traditional pathways may be limited. IMB missionary Ellie Bohrer teaches a 12th grade World Views class at Black Forest Academy in Germany. The IMB is seeking other educators, like Bohrer, who are willing to use their skills on the mission field. IMB Photo Scott Ray, IMB senior director of global deployment, noted that many missionary positions go unfilled simply because they fall outside traditional perceptions of missionary service. He said professional skills can provide both practical ministry support and access to countries where traditional missionary visas are difficult to obtain. Opportunities exist for finance professionals, veterinarians, medical workers, Send Relief personnel and others. Healthcare remains one of the most strategic areas in demand. Tom Hicks, IMB director of global health strategies, said many medical professionals have the wrong perception about mission work. “We do have an issue where people will select out because they don’t think that what they do is useful on the mission field,” he said. In reality, Hicks said many areas across the globe are increasingly seeking family medicine physicians, internists, pediatricians, pediatric nurse practitioners, OB providers, physical therapists, occupational therapists, speech pathologists and lactation consultants. The need is especially significant in sub-Saharan Africa, where young populations create a growing demand for pediatric care. Healthcare professionals also provide a unique advantage in countries that restrict missionary activity. “Missionaries with a vocational value, like healthcare missionaries, have opportunities to go places that others can’t go,” Hicks said. Another often-overlooked ministry is member care, which focuses on the spiritual, emotional, mental and relational health of IMB missionaries. Chris Martin is the IMB director of global member care. “Member care missionaries stand alongside those missionaries that are thought of traditionally as church planters or evangelists and support them,” Martin said. Many who serve in these roles come from counseling backgrounds and help missionaries navigate stress, conflict, grief and other challenges that can affect long-term ministry effectiveness. Martin compares their role to Aaron and Hur in Exodus 19, holding up Moses’ arms during battle, strengthening those serving on the front lines.
